epics.title: E04 — Knight Combat
epics.description:
## Outcome
Sword/shield gameplay supports attack chains, blocks, parries, dodges, stagger, heavy/charged attacks, shield bashes, weapon reach, armor trade-offs and satisfying hit reactions — and a greybox skeleton fight is fun with no rewards. The shared damage model underpins every class.

## Scope
- In: damage model (types, resistances, poise, modifiers), hit volumes, move data, action timeline, stamina, light chain, block, parry/riposte, dodge/i-frames, heavy/charged, shield bash, reach classes, armor weight, hit-stop, hit reactions, knight world verbs (smash, kick), environmental damage, creature attack hooks, combat sandbox, combat HUD, golden replays, assists, fun validation.
- Out: thief backstab/stealth attacks (thief group), spells (magic group), creature AI decisions (e11), bestiary content (e13), final animation/art/audio assets (art/audio group).

## Exit criteria
- All combat rules live in src/sim/combat with 100% coverage and golden replays.
- Skeleton fun validation spike passes, or its tuning beads are complete and a re-run passes.
- Combat sandbox covers every knight verb for manual tuning.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 src/sim/combat reports 100% coverage and the golden combat replay suite is green in CI.
- EC-2 docs/playtests/skeleton-fun-01.md (or a later re-run) records PASS against the stated bar.
- EC-3 A knight can break a weak wall, kick a brazier into flammables and shove a creature off a ledge in the greybox testbed without scripted pairings.

epics.title: E05 — Archery
epics.description:
## Outcome
Bows feel excellent; arrows have physical presence (gravity, drag, sticking, retrieval), weak points and elevation matter, and trick arrows (fire, water, rope, noise, blunt) solve problems through world properties rather than scripted pairings.

## Scope
- In: arrow schema, ballistics, draw/aim/release, focused release, sway, weak points, elevation, moving targets, retrieval, trick arrows, shootable/cuttable mechanisms, archery range, archer mobility.
- Out: arrow crafting/economy (e17/e20), creature reactions to noise (stealth group), final bow/arrow art/audio (asset group).

## Exit criteria
- Every trick arrow's effect is expressed via world-property emissions and validated by property-based tests.
- The archer can reach a high ledge, open a distant gate and douse a light in the greybox testbed.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Ballistics and bow rules in src/sim reach 100% coverage with deterministic replays.
- EC-2 An extended arrow can be added as data only (demonstrated by e05-trick-arrows-extended or a test fixture).
- EC-3 Median playtest rating for "the bow feels satisfying" ≥ 4/5.

epics.title: E28 — Audio & Combat Feedback
epics.description:
## Outcome
Weapons, spells, footsteps, creatures and environments have satisfying positional audio and feedback, driven by data from sim events, within the browser and performance baseline.

## Scope
- In: Web Audio engine, cue sheets, placeholder pack, combat/bow audio rules, footsteps, creature audio slots, mixer settings, snapshots/ducking, occlusion, reverb zones, ambience, adaptive music controller, sound captions, audio perf budgets.
- Out: creating final SFX/music (art/audio group via e38 prompt beads), stealth noise simulation (e09-sound-propagation), dialogue subtitles (dialogue group).

## Exit criteria
- Every gameplay event with feedback value has a cue rule; placeholder report shows the remaining gaps.
- Audio never influences sim determinism (verified by audio-on/off replay hash tests).
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 src/audio ≥ 90% coverage; audio on/off replays produce identical sim hashes.
- EC-2 Audio perf budgets are green in the e32 suite.
- EC-3 Sound captions cover all creature telegraphs and alert barks.

epics.title: E29 — VFX & Magical Spectacle
epics.description:
## Outcome
Magic, impacts, destruction, stealth feedback and environmental effects establish the game's visual identity, derived from sim events and world properties, within the particle and frame budgets.

## Scope
- In: VFX framework and budget manager, cue sheets, placeholders, hit sparks, screen feedback, weapon trails, spectacle shader library, elemental state visuals, destruction, spell VFX slots/templates, arrow effects, stealth indicators, decals, ambient effects, perf/auto-degrade.
- Out: final textures/flipbooks (asset group via e37 prompt beads), spell logic (e06), stealth HUD meters (stealth group).

## Exit criteria
- Element states and breakables are visualised automatically from properties.
- VFX stress scene meets the hardware baseline on High and Low.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 VFX stress scene p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High) and ≥ 30 fps on Low-class hardware.
- EC-2 Any spell can be visualised with templates only (demonstrated in the testbed).
- EC-3 VFX on/off replays produce identical sim hashes.

items.title: Deterministic damage model: damage types, resistances, poise, death
items.description:
## Why
Every class and creature must resolve harm through one rule set so knight swings, arrows, backstabs, spells and falling rocks compose systemically (Combat constitution; "enemies reward understanding behaviour" via weaknesses).

## What
A pure `src/sim/combat/damage` module. A `DamagePacket` carries `instigator`, `source`, per-type amounts (`slash`, `pierce`, `blunt`, `fire`, `frost`, `shock`, `arcane`, `poison`), `poiseDamage`, `staminaDamage`, `impulse`, `impactForce` and `tags` (e.g. `critical`, `backstab`, `weakpoint`, `riposte`, `environment`). Resolution runs an ordered **modifier pipeline**: attacker modifiers → hit-region multiplier → defender resistances → guard/block → armor flat absorption → clamp. Other groups register modifiers (e.g. thief backstab ×N, spell amplifiers) without editing core code. Components: `Health`, `Poise` (max, current, regen delay, regen rate), `Resistances`. Emits `DamageApplied` (with per-type breakdown), `PoiseBroken`, `Died` on the sim event bus. Amounts use integer hundredths to avoid float drift in replays.

## Scope
- In: Damage packet, damage types, resistance multipliers, modifier pipeline API, health, poise accumulation/regen, death event
- In: Zod schema fragment for resistances/poise reused by e12-creature-schema
- Out: Hit detection volumes (e04-hit-volumes)
- Out: Hit reaction selection (e04-hit-reactions)
- Out: Environmental damage sources (e04-environmental-damage)
- Out: Thief backstab rules (thief group, consumes modifier API)
- Out: Spell damage authoring (e06-spell-pipeline)

## Notes
Poise defaults: poise regenerates at 25% of max per second after 2.0 s (120 ticks) without poise damage. Resistance multipliers in [0, 3]; 0 = immune. Example: skeleton blunt 1.5, pierce 0.5, poison 0.
This is the anchor other groups depend on. Related: thief backstab bonus (e10), sorcerer spell damage (e06), archer weak points (e05-weak-points) all register modifiers here.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a defender with slash resistance 0.5 and no armor, when a 40-slash packet resolves, then health decreases by exactly 20.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a packet of 30 blunt + 20 fire against resistances blunt 1.5 / fire 1.0, when resolved, then total damage is 65 and `DamageApplied` lists the per-type breakdown {blunt: 45, fire: 20}.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two modifiers registered at stages `attacker` (×2 when tagged `backstab`) and `defender` (−10 flat), when a tagged 20-pierce packet resolves, then result is 30 and stage order is stable by (stage, registration id) across 1000 seeded runs.
- AC-4 [unit] Given poise max 50, when three 20-poise hits land within 120 ticks, then `PoiseBroken` is emitted exactly once on the third hit and poise resets to 50; given the same hits 150 ticks apart, then no break occurs because poise regenerated.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a creature with 5 health, when a 1000-damage packet resolves, then health clamps to 0, `Died` is emitted exactly once, and later packets on the dead entity are ignored (no second `Died`, no negative health).
- AC-6 [unit] Given a resistance of 0 for a damage type, when only that type is dealt, then 0 damage is applied and `DamageApplied.immune` is true so feedback can show "no effect".
- AC-7 [content] Given creature data with resistances, when validated, then unknown damage types or multipliers outside [0, 3] fail with the offending JSON path.
- AC-8 [unit] Given the combat sim module, when the coverage suite runs, then src/sim/combat/damage reports 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.

items.title: Swept hitboxes and region-tagged hurtboxes in the sim
items.description:
## Why
Hits must land where the player sees them land and never tunnel through fast swings; region tags make heads and weak points matter for every class.

## What
Sim-side collision shapes independent of the renderer: hurtboxes (capsule/sphere/box) attached to entity sockets with a region tag (`weakpoint` > `head` > `torso` > `limb`, plus `armored` flag) and multiplier; hitboxes driven by authored socket tracks from move data and **swept** from previous to current tick pose so a 2 m sword arc over 4 active ticks cannot skip a thin target. One hit per target per active window. Faction/friendly-fire rules per move so creatures can be tricked into hitting each other. The render animation follows sim poses, never the other way round.

## Scope
- In: Shape types, swept capsule tests, region priority, per-swing hit registry, friendly-fire flags
- In: Debug draw data exposed to the greybox testbed overlay
- Out: Projectile swept tests (e05-arrow-projectile reuses the query)
- Out: Animation authoring (render)

## Notes
Region priority resolves overlapping hurtboxes. Keep shape math in src/sim/geom so arrows and spells share it.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sword hitbox sweeping a 2.0 m arc over 4 active ticks and a 0.4 m-radius target capsule mid-arc that no single tick pose overlaps, when stepped, then exactly one hit registers on the tick whose sweep intersects it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hitbox overlapping the same target for all 4 active ticks, when stepped, then exactly one hit event is emitted for that swing and target.
- AC-3 [unit] Given overlapping head and torso hurtboxes both intersected on the same tick, when resolved, then the hit carries region `head` and its multiplier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a sweep crossing an ally with `friendlyFire: true` in the move, when stepped, then the ally is damaged; with `friendlyFire: false`, then the ally is ignored.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an attacker destroyed during its active window, when the next tick runs, then its hit volumes are removed and no further hits are emitted.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox testbed with the hitbox overlay enabled, when a swing plays, then the drawn shapes hash-match the sim shapes for every rendered frame.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 24 active hitboxes and 40 hurtboxes, when the hit query runs, then it takes ≤ 0.5 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.

items.title: Data schema for attack moves: frames, costs, hitboxes, flags, cues
items.description:
## Why
Combat must be data-driven so knights, creatures and archers share one move format and designers tune timing without code changes (Technical constitution).

## What
A zod schema for `MoveDef`: `id`, frame data (`startup`, `active`, `recovery` ticks), `cancelWindows` (into dodge/attack/block by tick range), `staminaCost`, damage packet template, `poiseDamage`, `staminaDamage`, hitbox track id, `reach` class, `swing` (`horizontal`|`vertical`|`thrust`), flags (`parryable`, `blockable`, `unblockable`, `hyperarmor` tick range + poise cap, `iframes` tick range, `interruptible`), `telegraphTick`, `chainNext`, and presentation ids (`anim`, `audioCue`, `vfxCue`). Initial data: knight sword light 1–3, heavy, charged, shield bash, kick, dodge roll, backstep; training-dummy swing.

## Scope
- In: Schema, validators, initial knight move file, loader to runtime tables
- Out: Executing moves (e04-action-timeline)
- Out: Creature-specific move sets (e13 bestiary, via e04-creature-attack-hooks)

## Notes
Unknown presentation cue ids warn (placeholder assets may lag) but never fail validation.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the knight move file, when validated, then all moves pass and `sword-light-1` resolves to startup 12 / active 4 / recovery 18 ticks.
- AC-2 [content] Given a move whose i-frame or hyperarmor range extends beyond startup+active+recovery, when validated, then it fails with the move id and field path.
- AC-3 [content] Given a move whose `chainNext` references a missing move id, when validated, then it fails listing the dangling reference.
- AC-4 [content] Given a move flagged both `parryable` and `unblockable` without `parryable` override note, when validated, then a warning is emitted (legal but unusual).
- AC-5 [content] Given a move with an unknown `audioCue` id, when validated, then validation passes with one warning naming the id.

items.title: Action timeline FSM with input buffer, cancel windows and local time
items.description:
## Why
Souls-like weight comes from committed startup/active/recovery phases; a fair 150 ms input buffer keeps that weight from feeling unresponsive.

## What
A deterministic per-entity action state machine that executes `MoveDef`s: phases, cancel windows, chain transitions, interruption by hit reactions, and a per-entity **local time scale** (used for hit-stop). Input buffer: an action pressed up to 9 ticks (150 ms) before it becomes legal executes on the first legal tick; the most recent buffered input wins. Consumes abstract actions from e02-input-actions, never raw keys.

## Scope
- In: Timeline runner, buffer, cancel rules, interrupt API, local time scale, action-rejected events
- Out: Specific knight moves and their tuning (e04-melee-core and siblings)
- Out: Hit-stop amounts (e04-hit-stop)

## Notes
Stamina is spent on the first startup tick and is not refunded if interrupted (souls convention).
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a move with startup 12 / active 4 / recovery 18, when executed from tick 0, then phase transitions occur at ticks 12, 16 and 34 exactly.
- AC-2 [unit] Given attack pressed 8 ticks before recovery ends, when recovery ends, then the chained move starts that tick; given it pressed 12 ticks before, then the input is dropped.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a move with a dodge cancel window starting at recovery tick 6, when dodge is pressed at recovery tick 4, then the dodge executes on recovery tick 6.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity interrupted during startup, when the interrupt resolves, then no hitbox spawns and the stamina already spent is not refunded.
- AC-5 [unit] Given local time scale 0 for 4 ticks during an active phase, when time resumes, then the phase continues from the same offset and total move duration is extended by exactly 4 ticks.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a recorded input log of a 3-hit chain with a dodge cancel, when replayed 100 times through e00-replay-harness, then every tick's state hash is identical.

items.title: Stamina pool governs attacks, blocks, dodges and sprint
items.description:
## Why
Stamina gives fights rhythm — attack, breathe, defend — which is the backbone of weighty souls-like combat.

## What
As a knight, I want a stamina bar that my attacks, blocks, dodges and sprinting draw from so that fights have a readable push-and-pull rhythm.
Max 100. Regenerates 40/s after a 30-tick (500 ms) delay since the last spend; while blocking regen ×0.35. Costs come from move data. An action is allowed whenever stamina > 0 and may drive it to 0 (the "last action" rule). Reaching 0 triggers **Exhausted**: regen delay becomes 72 ticks (1.2 s) and sprint is disabled until stamina ≥ 20. Sprint drains 10/s.

## Scope
- In: Stamina component, regen rules, exhaustion, action gating, `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` event
- Out: HUD bar (e04-hud-vitals)
- Out: Armor-weight regen modifiers (e04-armor-weight)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 100 stamina, when a 12-cost attack starts, then stamina is 88 and does not regenerate for 30 ticks, after which it rises 40/s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 5 stamina, when a 20-cost dodge is requested, then it executes and stamina becomes 0 (not negative) and Exhausted is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 0 stamina, when attack is pressed, then the action is rejected and `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` is emitted once per press.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an Exhausted knight, when sprint is held, then sprint is refused until stamina ≥ 20.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a knight holding block, when 60 ticks pass after the regen delay, then stamina regenerates at 14/s (40 × 0.35).
- AC-6 [manual] Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when a playtester fights the attacker dummy, then they can describe when they are "out of breath" without looking at the HUD (audio + animation cues suffice).

items.title: Knight light attack chain and shield block with guard break
items.description:
## Why
This is the first playable fight of the vertical slice: a sword chain that feels weighty and a shield that makes defence a choice (Knight fantasy: weight, impact, mastery).

## What
As a knight, I want a three-hit sword chain and a shield block so that I can trade blows deliberately and defend against frontal attacks.
Chain: L1 12/4/18 ticks, 12 stamina, 20 slash, 15 poise; L2 10/4/20, 14 stamina, 22 slash, 15 poise; L3 16/5/26, 18 stamina, 30 slash, 30 poise. The chain resets to L1 after 30 idle ticks past recovery. During startup the knight may rotate up to 360°/s toward the lock-on target (from e02-camera); during active frames rotation is locked (commitment).
Block (hold): shield becomes active after 6 ticks (100 ms); covers a frontal 120° arc; movement at 50% speed. Wood shield absorbs 85% physical / 30% fire, stability 60: stamina loss = attack `staminaDamage` × (1 − stability/100). If stamina reaches 0 while blocking, **Guard Break**: 60-tick stagger, `GuardBroken` event, and the unabsorbed remainder of that hit applies.

## Scope
- In: Light chain, block, guard break, lock-on tracking during startup, initial wood shield data
- Out: Parry and riposte (e04-parry-riposte)
- Out: Dodge (e04-dodge-iframes)
- Out: Heavy/charged (e04-heavy-charged)
- Out: Shield bash (e04-shield-bash)

## Notes
Anchor e04-melee-core: this item delivers the minimum fight for M1. Parry and dodge (also in the anchor's meaning) land as sibling items e04-parry-riposte and e04-dodge-iframes so dependents are not blocked on them.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an idle knight with 100 stamina, when attack is pressed three times inside each buffer window, then L1→L2→L3 execute, 44 stamina is spent, and the next press starts L1 again.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight whose shield has been raised ≥ 6 ticks, when a frontal 30-slash hit with staminaDamage 20 lands, then health drops by 4.5 and stamina by 8.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a blocking knight, when a hit arrives from outside the frontal 120° arc, then full damage applies and no stamina is drained by the block.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the shield raised only 3 ticks, when a frontal hit lands, then the block is not yet active and full damage applies.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a blocking knight with 8 stamina, when a hit with staminaDamage 20 lands, then stamina is 0, `GuardBroken` is emitted, the knight is staggered for 60 ticks and the unabsorbed damage is applied.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the combat sandbox dummy, when L1 connects, then `DamageApplied` appears on the sim event bus on a tick within L1's active window (ticks 12–15).
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, when Playwright issues the attack action three times, then the dummy's health drops by 72 (20+22+30) and no console errors are logged.
- AC-8 [manual] Given a 5-minute sandbox session, when three playtesters use the chain, then median rating for "swings feel heavy and committed" is ≥ 4/5 and none describe attacks as floaty.

items.title: Sim-chosen hit reactions: flinch, stagger, knockback, knockdown
items.description:
## Why
Readable reactions tell the player what their hit did; knockback into ledges and hazards lets combat interact with the world.

## What
As a player, I want enemies (and me) to react differently to light hits, poise breaks and heavy impacts so that I can read the fight and exploit openings.
The sim selects a reaction tier from poise state, hyperarmor and impulse: `none` (hyperarmor absorbed), `flinch` 12 ticks (interrupts startup only), `stagger` 45 ticks (on `PoiseBroken`), `knockback` 60 ticks + physics displacement (impulse ≥ 300 N·s equivalent), `knockdown` 90 ticks grounded then wake-up with 20 i-frame ticks. Direction quadrant (front/back/left/right) from hit vector vs facing. Creature schema may override tiers (e.g. trolls never knocked down). Displacement goes through physics so a shoved creature can fall off ledges or into fire.

## Scope
- In: Reaction selection, durations, direction, displacement via physics, `HitReaction` event with reaction id for render/audio
- Out: Animation assets (render/art)
- Out: Critical/riposte states (e04-parry-riposte)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with 40 poise and no hyperarmor, when a 15-poise hit lands during its startup, then a 12-tick flinch interrupts the attack.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hit that emits `PoiseBroken`, when resolved, then the reaction is `stagger` for 45 ticks and the victim's current action is cancelled.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hit from behind the victim, when resolved, then the reaction direction is `back`; given a hit at 80° to the right, then `right`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a victim in a hyperarmor window with remaining cap 40 and a 30-poise hit, when resolved, then reaction is `none` but damage still applies.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a creature standing 0.5 m from a ledge in the greybox testbed, when a knockback hit lands toward the ledge, then the creature falls off and environmental fall damage rules apply.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a knocked-down entity, when it wakes up, then it is invulnerable for 20 ticks and cannot be re-knocked-down during them.

items.title: Dodge roll and backstep with invulnerability frames
items.description:
## Why
A precise dodge with honest i-frames is the souls-like skill expression that makes dangerous enemies fair.

## What
As a knight, I want to roll through or away from attacks with a short invulnerability window so that timing, not stats, keeps me alive.
Roll (directional, relative to camera or lock-on): 36 ticks, 20 stamina, i-frames ticks 2–14 (13 ticks ≈ 217 ms) at medium defaults, 3.0 m travel. Backstep (no direction held): 24 ticks, 12 stamina, i-frames 2–7. Roll recovery cancellable into a roll-attack from tick 28. Hits landing during i-frames apply no damage, poise or reaction and emit `DodgedHit` (feedback + telemetry). Rolling off ledges is allowed; rolling into a wall stops displacement but i-frames continue.

## Scope
- In: Roll, backstep, i-frames, roll-attack cancel, `DodgedHit` event
- Out: Load-class variations (e04-armor-weight)
- Out: Archer quickstep (e05-mobile-archery)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a roll started on tick 0, when a hit lands on tick 14, then no damage/poise applies and `DodgedHit` is emitted; when a hit lands on tick 15, then it applies normally.
- AC-2 [unit] Given no movement input, when dodge is pressed, then a backstep executes costing 12 stamina with i-frames on ticks 2–7 only.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a roll toward a wall 1 m away, when stepped, then displacement stops at the wall and i-frames still run through tick 14.
- AC-4 [unit] Given attack pressed at roll tick 26 (inside the buffer), when tick 28 arrives, then the roll-attack move starts.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a replay of the attacker dummy swinging and a roll timed 1 tick early vs on time, when replayed, then outcomes differ exactly as recorded and hashes are deterministic across 100 runs.
- AC-6 [manual] Given the sandbox attacker dummy, when three playtesters practise for 3 minutes, then each reports dodges "felt fair" (no hits they believed they had dodged) — any counterexample is logged with a replay file.

items.title: Combat sandbox scene with dummy creatures and frame-data overlay
items.description:
## Why
Combat feel is tuned by iteration; a dedicated sandbox makes every timing change testable in seconds and gives e2e tests a stable arena.

## What
As a developer, I want a combat sandbox scene with configurable dummies and live frame data so that I can tune and verify timing without playing through levels.
Contents: a training dummy (infinite-health toggle, configurable resistances/poise/hurtbox regions), an attacker dummy that performs a selected move on a metronome (default every 2.0 s; parryable/unblockable toggle) for parry and dodge practice, a frame-data overlay (current move, phase, tick, i-frame/hyperarmor highlights, hitboxes/hurtboxes), DPS/poise readouts, debug slow-motion (sim steps at 0.25× wall time; sim tick count unchanged), and spawners via e33-debug-console.

## Scope
- In: Scene, dummies, overlay, slow-mo, console commands
- In: Deterministic scene seed for e2e tests
- Out: Archery range layout (e05-archery-range)
- Out: Real creature AI (e11)

## Notes
Scene is loaded via e00-greybox-testbed's scene loader under /dev/combat.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the sandbox, when `spawn dummy --poise 60 --resist slash=0.5` is entered, then a dummy with those values exists in sim state.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the attacker dummy set to a 2.0 s metronome, when 10 s elapse, then exactly 5 swings start, each on a tick multiple of 120.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the sandbox loaded in Chromium, when the frame overlay is toggled, then it shows move id, phase and tick matching sim state and no console errors occur.
- AC-4 [unit] Given slow-motion 0.25×, when 4 s of wall time pass, then exactly 60 sim ticks have run and frame data is unchanged versus normal speed.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a dummy with infinite health, when 10,000 damage is dealt, then it never emits `Died` and health display resets after 3 s.

items.title: Combat HUD: health and stamina bars with damage feedback
items.description:
## Why
The player must read health and stamina at a glance without numbers cluttering the screen (Zelda-like readability).

## What
As a player, I want clear health and stamina bars and a hint of where damage came from so that I can make decisions mid-fight.
Health bar with delayed "chip" segment (lost health shown in a lighter colour that drains after 500 ms); stamina bar that flashes when an action is rejected for stamina; low-health pulse below 25%; off-screen damage direction indicator (arc toward source for 1.5 s); HUD scale from settings. UI reads sim state through the game layer only — no rules in UI.

## Scope
- In: Health/stamina bars, chip, rejection flash, low-health pulse, damage direction indicator, HUD scale setting
- Out: Target/lock-on HUD (e04-hud-target)
- Out: Screen shake/vignette (e29-screen-feedback)
- Out: Stealth HUD (stealth group)

## Notes
Placeholder UI art until the style bible (e37-style-bible) lands; integration of final UI art is a separate asset bead.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given health 100→70 on one hit, when rendered, then the bar shows 70 filled and a 30-wide chip segment that begins draining at 500 ms and is gone by 1000 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an `ActionRejected{reason:"stamina"}` event, when processed, then the stamina bar enters its flash state for 300 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hit from a source 120° behind the camera forward, when processed, then the damage indicator arc points to 120° and fades out at 1.5 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given health at 24% of max, when rendered, then the low-health pulse is active; at 25% it is not.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the combat sandbox, when the player takes a dummy hit, then the DOM/engine HUD health value matches sim health within one rendered frame.
- AC-6 [unit] Given HUD scale set to 150% in settings, when the HUD mounts, then bar dimensions are 1.5× baseline and remain within the viewport at 1280×720.

items.title: Hit-stop freezes attacker and victim briefly on impact
items.description:
## Why
A few frames of freeze on impact is the single biggest contributor to perceived weight in melee combat.

## What
As a knight, I want a tiny freeze when my blade connects so that every hit feels like it met resistance.
Per-entity local time freeze (via e04-action-timeline) for attacker and victim only: light 3 ticks (50 ms), heavy 5 (83 ms), charged 6, parry 8 (133 ms), riposte/critical 10. Other entities, projectiles and the world keep running. Overlapping freezes take the max, never the sum; multi-target hits freeze once.

## Scope
- In: Freeze durations by hit tier, stacking rule, event for presentation sync (audio/VFX start on first frozen frame)
- Out: Camera shake (e29-screen-feedback)

## Notes
Hit-stop is a sim rule because it shifts action timing; it is recorded in replays. Reduce-motion settings affect camera shake, not hit-stop.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a heavy attack connecting on tick 20, when stepped, then attacker and victim local time are 0 for ticks 20–24 and resume on tick 25.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a third creature attacking during that freeze, when stepped, then its timeline advances normally.
- AC-3 [unit] Given one heavy swing hitting three enemies on the same tick, when stepped, then the attacker freezes 5 ticks total, not 15.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a victim already frozen 3 ticks by one hit and hit by a parry-tier event, when stepped, then remaining freeze becomes 8 ticks (max), not 11.
- AC-5 [manual] Given A/B builds with hit-stop on vs off, when three playtesters try both blind, then at least two of three prefer hit-stop on for "impact".

items.title: Parry window and riposte critical attack
items.description:
## Why
Parrying is the knight's mastery verb: high risk, high reward, readable windows (Knight fantasy: mastery).

## What
As a knight, I want to parry a well-timed attack and punish it with a riposte so that learning enemy rhythms is rewarded.
Parry: 30-tick action, 10 stamina, **active window ticks 4–13 (10 ticks ≈ 167 ms)**. A `parryable` hit landing in the window: defender takes 0 damage and 0 stamina loss, attacker enters **Parried** for 90 ticks (1.5 s), 8-tick hit-stop. Failed parry (no hit in window): ticks 14–30 are vulnerable and a hit there is a counter-hit (×1.25 damage). Unparryable moves (`parryable: false`, grabs, most spells) pass through as normal hits. **Riposte**: attack pressed while a Parried target is within 2.0 m and within the knight's frontal 60°: critical move (3× base damage, tagged `critical`/`riposte`, ignores poise) with i-frames for its duration. Parry window values are data-driven so progression (e19) and assists (e04-combat-assists) can widen them.

## Scope
- In: Parry action, window, Parried state, counter-hit rule, riposte critical move
- Out: Parrying projectiles (P3 idea, see Notes)
- Out: Thief backstab critical (thief group; shares `critical` tag and the modifier API)

## Notes
Idea for post-MVP: deflecting arrows with a perfect parry. Related: progression upgrades that widen the window (e19).
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given parry pressed on tick 0, when a parryable hit lands on tick 4 or tick 13, then it is parried; on tick 3 or tick 14, then it is not.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a successful parry, when resolved, then the defender loses 0 health and 0 stamina and the attacker is Parried for exactly 90 ticks.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a Parried target 1.8 m away in the frontal 60°, when attack is pressed, then the riposte move executes and deals 3× base damage tagged `critical` and `riposte`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a Parried target 2.2 m away, when attack is pressed, then a normal L1 executes instead of a riposte.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a failed parry, when a hit lands on tick 20, then damage is multiplied by 1.25 and tagged `counter`.
- AC-6 [unit] Given an `unparryable` move, when it lands inside the parry window, then it applies as a normal unblocked hit.
- AC-7 [integration] Given golden replays of parry-on-first-tick, parry-on-last-tick and parry-one-tick-late, when replayed, then outcomes match the fixtures exactly.
- AC-8 [manual] Given the sandbox attacker dummy with a 2 s metronome, when three playtesters practise for 5 minutes, then each lands ≥ 5 parries and rates the window "learnable" ≥ 4/5.

items.title: Heavy and charged attacks with hyperarmor
items.description:
## Why
Heavy and charged attacks give the knight a committed, high-impact option that breaks poise and walls (weight, impact, stagger).

## What
As a knight, I want a heavy attack I can charge so that I can gamble time for a stagger or a smashed wall.
Heavy: 24/5/26 ticks, 25 stamina, 1.6× damage, 2.2× poise damage, hyperarmor ticks 10–29 absorbing up to 40 poise. Charged: hold heavy up to 60 ticks (1 s); damage multiplier lerps 1.0→1.8 and poise 2.2→3.5×; `ChargeReady` event at full charge; auto-release at 90 ticks; total stamina 25 + 10 at full charge. Released before 12 ticks of hold = normal heavy. If hyperarmor is broken during charge, the charge is lost. Every heavy/charged hit carries `impactForce` (used by e04-smash-breakables).

## Scope
- In: Heavy move, charge hold, multipliers, hyperarmor, impactForce values
- Out: Breaking objects (e04-smash-breakables)
- Out: Charge VFX (e29-weapon-trails) and cue (e28-combat-hit-audio)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given heavy held for 60 ticks and released, when it connects, then damage is 1.8× base and poise damage 3.5× base, and 35 stamina was spent.
- AC-2 [unit] Given heavy released after 8 ticks of hold, when resolved, then it behaves as an uncharged heavy (1.6×/2.2×).
- AC-3 [unit] Given heavy held for 90 ticks, when tick 90 arrives, then it auto-releases at full charge.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a charging knight with hyperarmor cap 40, when a 30-poise hit lands, then no reaction occurs; when a further 15-poise hit lands, then the knight staggers and the charge is lost.
- AC-5 [unit] Given full charge reached, when the tick completes, then exactly one `ChargeReady` event is emitted.
- AC-6 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters use charged attacks against a 60-poise dummy, then each can reliably stagger it and rates the payoff ≥ 4/5.

items.title: Shield bash interrupts, shoves and breaks bashable objects
items.description:
## Why
The shield should be a tool, not just a wall: interrupting casters and shoving things fits the knight's physical-world fantasy.

## What
As a knight, I want to bash with my shield while blocking so that I can interrupt enemies, break weak guards and shove objects.
Bash (attack while blocking): 14/4/20 ticks, 18 stamina, 5 blunt, 45 poise damage, forward impulse. Interrupts any target currently in a move flagged `interruptible` (e.g. spell windups). Against shieldless blockers it causes Guard Break. Applies impulse to physics objects ≤ 60 kg and `impactForce` to `breakable` objects (e.g. flimsy barricades). Without a shield equipped, the input falls back to kick (e04-kick-verb).

## Scope
- In: Bash move, interrupt rule, guard-break-vs-shieldless, physics impulse, impactForce
- Out: Kick (e04-kick-verb)
- Out: Breakable toughness rules (e04-smash-breakables)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature in an `interruptible` windup, when a bash connects, then its move is cancelled and it flinches.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a shieldless creature blocking, when a bash connects, then it is Guard Broken for 60 ticks.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 30 kg barrel in front of the knight, when a bash connects, then the barrel is displaced ≥ 1.0 m by physics; given a 100 kg crate, then it does not move and a `ImpactResisted` event fires.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no shield equipped, when block+attack is pressed, then the kick move executes instead.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 10 stamina, when bash is requested, then it executes (last-action rule) and stamina becomes 0.

items.title: Weapon reach classes and swing-type wall recoil
items.description:
## Why
Weapon choice should change how you fight in a space — a halberd rules a hall but clangs off corridor walls (positioning, weapon reach).

## What
As a knight, I want weapons with different reach and swing types so that my choice of weapon matters in tight corridors versus open halls.
Reach classes (data): `short` 1.2 m (dagger/mace, fast 8/3/12), `medium` 2.0 m (sword), `long` 3.0 m (spear thrust, halberd sweep). **Wall recoil**: a `horizontal` swing from a medium/long weapon whose hitbox strikes `solid` static geometry during the first half of its active window before any creature → 30-tick recoil, `WallRecoil` event (sparks/clang). `vertical` and `thrust` swings never recoil. Weapon stats (reach, moveset, damage types) come from item data via e17-inventory-core.

## Scope
- In: Reach class data, swing types, recoil rule, three starter weapons (sword, spear, mace)
- Out: Weapon loot/placement (e18)
- Out: Weapon models (art)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a spear thrust with 3.0 m reach, when a target stands at 2.8 m, then it is hit; with a sword (2.0 m), then it is not.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a halberd horizontal sweep in a 2 m-wide greybox corridor, when swung, then `WallRecoil` fires and the knight is locked in recoil for 30 ticks.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the same corridor, when a spear thrust or vertical sword swing is used, then no recoil occurs.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a horizontal sweep that hits a creature before the wall on the same tick, when resolved, then the creature is hit and no recoil occurs.
- AC-5 [content] Given weapon item data, when validated, then every weapon declares a reach class and a moveset whose moves exist.

items.title: Armor weight sets roll class, stamina regen, poise and noise
items.description:
## Why
Armor must be a trade-off — protection and poise versus agility and stealth — not a bigger number (anti-grind rule).

## What
As a knight, I want heavier armor to protect me and hold my ground while slowing my rolls so that I choose a playstyle, not just a stat.
Load ratio = equipped weight / capacity. Light ≤ 30%: roll 3.6 m, i-frames 13, 36 ticks. Medium ≤ 70%: 3.0 m, 11 i-frames, 40 ticks. Heavy ≤ 100%: 2.2 m, 9 i-frames, 46 ticks, stamina regen ×0.85. Overloaded > 100%: no roll (stumble 20 ticks), walk only. Armor pieces add flat per-type absorption and poise bonus. Armor exposes a `noiseMultiplier` property (plate 1.6, chain 1.3, leather 1.0) consumed by stealth sound propagation.

## Scope
- In: Load classes, roll variants, regen modifier, absorption/poise from armor, noise multiplier property
- Out: Stealth noise simulation (e09-sound-propagation)
- Out: Armor items and art (e17/e18/art)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given load ratio exactly 30%, when a roll executes, then it uses the light profile; at 30.1%, then the medium profile.
- AC-2 [unit] Given heavy load, when a roll executes, then it lasts 46 ticks, travels 2.2 m and has 9 i-frame ticks.
- AC-3 [unit] Given load ratio 105%, when dodge is pressed, then a 20-tick stumble plays with no i-frames and sprint is disabled.
- AC-4 [unit] Given plate chest with 12 flat slash absorption, when a 30-slash hit lands, then 18 damage applies after resistances.
- AC-5 [integration] Given plate armor equipped, when the player walks, then emitted footstep noise events carry multiplier 1.6.

items.title: Smash breakable walls and objects by impact force
items.description:
## Why
"The knight might discover that an old wall can simply be smashed apart." Force-based breaking turns the knight's strength into a world verb (Classes change possibilities).

## What
As a knight, I want to smash cracked walls, barricades and crates with heavy blows so that brute force opens routes other classes find differently.
Any object with world property `breakable` and a `toughness` breaks when a single hit's `impactForce` ≥ toughness. impactForce = move base × charge multiplier × weapon class (blunt ×1.5). Hits below toughness advance a visible crack stage (max 2) but never break it — a readable hint that more force is needed. Breaking spawns debris physics objects, emits a loud noise event for stealth, can reveal passages, and persists via e27-world-state-store. The rule is property-based: any source dealing impactForce (bash, blunt arrow, gust spell, rolling boulder) works.

## Scope
- In: Toughness rule, crack stages, debris spawn, noise event, persistence
- Out: Destruction visuals (e29-destruction-fx)
- Out: Placing weak walls in levels (e26 dungeon)

## Notes
Suggested toughness: crate 20, barricade 60, weak masonry wall 110 (charged heavy blunt or equivalent only).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any `breakable` object with toughness 110, when a hit with impactForce 120 lands, then it breaks and `ObjectBroken` is emitted with the instigator.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same object, when a hit with impactForce 60 lands, then its crack stage increments (capped at 2) and it does not break.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a weak wall hiding a passage, when broken, then debris physics objects spawn, the passage collider is traversable and a noise event of loudness ≥ 80 is emitted.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a broken wall, when the game is saved and reloaded, then the wall remains broken.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a non-knight source (e.g. a blunt projectile) producing impactForce ≥ toughness, when it hits, then the object breaks identically (no class check).
- AC-6 [manual] Given a greybox room with one cracked wall, when three fresh playtesters play as knight, then at least two try hitting it within 2 minutes without being told.

items.title: Kick verb shoves creatures and physics objects
items.description:
## Why
Kicking over a brazier into oil or a barrel down stairs is the kind of improvised "wait, I can do that?" moment the world should reward.

## What
As a knight, I want to kick objects and enemies so that I can knock braziers over, send barrels rolling and shove foes off ledges.
Kick: 10/3/16 ticks, 8 stamina, 20 poise damage, 3 blunt, impulse to physics objects ≤ 40 kg; small creatures (schema size `small`) receive knockback. Kicking an unlocked, closed door swings it open hard: a creature behind it takes blunt damage and flinches. Consequences flow from properties: a kicked `burning` brazier carries fire to `flammable` surfaces via e03-element-propagation — no bespoke pairings.

## Scope
- In: Kick move, object impulse, door slam, small-creature knockback
- Out: Fire spread rules (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: Door locking (e03-doors-locks-switches)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a 25 kg object, when kicked, then it receives an impulse and moves ≥ 1.5 m on flat ground; given a 50 kg object, then it does not move.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a `burning` brazier next to a `flammable` rug, when the brazier is kicked over onto it, then the rug ignites via element propagation within 2 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an unlocked closed door with a creature 0.5 m behind it, when kicked, then the door opens and the creature takes blunt damage and flinches.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a locked door, when kicked, then it stays closed and emits `ImpactResisted` plus a noise event.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a `small` creature at a ledge, when kicked toward it, then it is knocked back over the ledge.

items.title: Fall, crush and hazard damage through the damage model
items.description:
## Why
Shoving a goblin off a bridge or dropping a chandelier on a troll must work through the same rules as swords (systemic world, multiple solutions).

## What
As a player, I want falls, falling objects and hazards to hurt anything they hit so that the environment is a weapon for every class.
Fall damage: none below 4 m, linear from 4 m (0%) to 14 m (100% max health), lethal above 14 m unless landing in deep water. Kinetic impacts: physics objects striking a creature at relative speed > 6 m/s deal blunt = 0.5·m·v² / 20 (tunable) with impactForce. Fire volumes deal 8 fire/s and apply `burning` per creature rules. All sources build a `DamagePacket` tagged `environment` with the instigator set to whoever caused it (for credit and AI blame).

## Scope
- In: Fall damage, kinetic impact damage, hazard volume damage, instigator attribution
- Out: Fire/water propagation rules (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: Trap design (thief group)

## Notes
Instigator chains let AI blame the player for a dropped chandelier (Related: e11 AI reactions).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 9 m fall, when the entity lands, then it takes 50% of max health as damage.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a 16 m fall into water ≥ 1.5 m deep, when landing, then no fall damage applies.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 40 kg chandelier dropped 5 m onto a creature, when it hits, then blunt damage is dealt with the instigator set to the entity that cut its rope.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with fire resistance 0 standing in a fire volume, when 3 s pass, then it takes 0 fire damage (immunity respected).
- AC-5 [unit] Given an object moving at 5 m/s touching a creature, when resolved, then no damage is dealt (below threshold).

items.title: Creatures attack via the move system with readable telegraphs
items.description:
## Why
Enemies are creatures, not dummies: their attacks must share the player's rules (parry, block, poise) and telegraph clearly for Zelda-like readability.

## What
As a designer, I want creature attacks defined as move data with enforced telegraphs so that every creature is parryable, dodgeable and readable by the same rules as the player.
Creature schema references moves; the combat layer exposes `canUseMove`, `rangeFor(move)`, cooldowns and `inRange` queries for AI (e11). Readability rules: every creature attack has a windup ≥ 18 ticks (300 ms) before active frames; `unblockable`/grab moves ≥ 30 ticks (500 ms) and must declare a distinct telegraph cue (audio + VFX). `TelegraphStarted` event fires on the move's `telegraphTick`.

## Scope
- In: Creature move references, AI query API, telegraph rules/events, greybox skeleton 3-move set for validation
- Out: AI decision-making (e11)
- Out: Bestiary content (e13)
- Out: Creature animation/art

## Notes
Greybox skeleton moves: overhead chop (parryable), 2-hit slash (parryable), lunging thrust (unparryable, blockable). Related: bestiary skeleton (e13) should adopt these.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a creature move with startup 12 ticks, when validated, then it fails the readability rule (minimum 18).
- AC-2 [content] Given an `unblockable` creature move with no telegraph cue or startup < 30 ticks, when validated, then it fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature executing a move with telegraphTick 4, when tick 4 runs, then exactly one `TelegraphStarted` event is emitted with the move's cue ids.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature move on cooldown 120 ticks, when `canUseMove` is queried at tick 60, then it returns false with reason `cooldown`.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox skeleton's overhead chop, when the knight parries it in the window, then the skeleton enters Parried exactly as the dummy does.

items.title: Lock-on reticle, target health/poise bar and hit markers
items.description:
## Why
Players need to see who they are locked onto and whether their hits matter (poise, immunity) without number spam.

## What
As a player, I want a lock-on reticle and a target health/poise readout so that I know my target and how close it is to breaking.
Reticle on the lock-on target from e02-camera; target health bar with chip; poise bar appears after first poise damage and flashes on `PoiseBroken`; "no effect" indicator when `DamageApplied.immune`; boss bar docked at bottom for creatures flagged `boss`; hit marker variants (normal, weak point, headshot, deflected). Damage numbers exist as an option, off by default.

## Scope
- In: Reticle, target bars, immune indicator, boss bar, hit markers, damage-number option
- Out: Lock-on targeting logic (e02-camera)
- Out: Final UI art (asset beads)

## Notes
Hit marker variants are also used by archery (e05-weak-points).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a lock-on target, when rendered, then the reticle is anchored to its lock-on socket and hidden when no target exists.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the target dies, when `Died` is processed, then the reticle and target bar hide within one rendered frame.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `DamageApplied.immune` on the target, when processed, then a "no effect" indicator shows for 800 ms and no chip appears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature flagged `boss` enters combat, when processed, then the boss bar shows its display name and health at the bottom of the screen.
- AC-5 [unit] Given damage numbers disabled (default), when damage occurs, then no numbers render; enabled, then the number equals the applied total.

items.title: Golden replay suite for combat timing boundaries
items.description:
## Why
Timing windows are the game; golden replays guarantee a refactor never silently shifts a parry by one tick.

## What
A set of recorded input logs + expected state hashes in `tests/replays/combat/`: 3-hit chain; parry first/last/one-late tick; guard break; i-frame boundary (tick 14 vs 15); charged release at 11/12/60/90 ticks; hit-stop stacking; wall recoil. CI runs them on every PR; a failure prints the first divergent tick and the differing component.

## Scope
- In: Fixtures, CI wiring, divergence reporter, fixture re-record script with review checklist
- Out: Replay harness itself (e00-replay-harness)

## Notes
Re-recording a fixture requires a PR note explaining the intended timing change.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the combat fixtures, when run in CI, then all replays match their stored hashes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a deliberate 1-tick change to the parry window, when the suite runs, then the parry-last-tick fixture fails and reports the first divergent tick and component `ParryState`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given src/sim/combat, when coverage runs, then it reports 100% on all metrics.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a fixture recorded with an older move-data version, when run, then the harness fails with a clear "fixture data version mismatch" message rather than a hash diff.

items.title: Combat assist settings: wider parry, extra i-frames, stamina
items.description:
## Why
Accessibility: more players should reach the joy of a parry without removing the skill ceiling for others.

## What
As a player, I want optional combat assists so that timing-heavy combat is accessible to me.
Options via e31-settings-framework: parry window ×1.0/×1.5/×2.0 (extends the end tick), i-frames +0/+3/+6 ticks, stamina costs ×1.0/×0.75, extended creature telegraph cue (+10 ticks warning). Values are injected into the sim at session start and recorded in the replay header for determinism.

## Scope
- In: Assist options, sim injection, replay header recording, settings UI entries
- Out: Difficulty levels / enemy damage scaling (later if needed)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given parry assist ×2.0, when parry is pressed on tick 0, then hits on ticks 4–23 are parried (window 20 ticks).
- AC-2 [unit] Given i-frame assist +3, when a medium-load roll executes, then i-frames cover ticks 2–17.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a replay recorded with assists on, when replayed on a machine with assists off, then the header values are used and hashes match.
- AC-4 [unit] Given assists changed mid-session, when applied, then they take effect at the next safe point (no action in progress) and an `AssistsChanged` event is logged.

items.title: Validate a greybox skeleton fight is fun with no rewards
items.description:
## Why
Constitution: "Fighting a skeleton should be enjoyable even when the player doesn't need XP or loot." This spike proves or disproves that before content scales.

## What
Question: with placeholder art/audio, is repeatedly fighting a greybox skeleton (3-move set from e04-creature-attack-hooks) intrinsically enjoyable for the knight with zero XP/loot? Time-box: 2 days. Protocol: ≥ 5 playtesters (internal acceptable), short tutorial, then an arena that spawns a new skeleton on demand; observe, record replays and telemetry (parries, dodges, voluntary re-fights, session length), short survey.

## Scope
- In: Test protocol, arena variant of the sandbox, telemetry events, write-up with tuning recommendations
- Out: Implementing the recommendations (follow-up beads)
- Out: External m4 playtests (e35)

## Notes
Pass bar: ≥ 4 of 5 testers voluntarily fight ≥ 3 skeletons beyond the required one and median "fun" ≥ 4/5. Failing is a valid outcome and must produce concrete tuning beads. Related: e13 bestiary skeleton, e35 fun validation.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given ≥ 5 playtest sessions, when completed, then docs/playtests/skeleton-fun-01.md records per-tester voluntary re-fight counts, fun rating (1–5) and quotes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the arena build, when a session runs, then telemetry events for parry attempts/successes, dodges, deaths and re-fights are exported via e34-telemetry-events.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the results, when compared to the pass bar (≥ 4/5 testers fight ≥ 3 extra skeletons; median fun ≥ 4), then the write-up states PASS or FAIL explicitly.
- AC-4 [manual] Given a FAIL or any rating ≤ 2, when the write-up is finished, then at least three tuning beads are proposed with the replay files that motivated them.

items.title: Data schema for arrow types and property-based payloads
items.description:
## Why
Trick arrows must act through world properties, not scripted pairings, so a new arrow is data and interactions emerge (architectural principle).

## What
A zod schema for `ArrowDef`: `id`, `mass_g`, `dragK`, base `DamagePacket` template, `penetration`, `onImpact` (`stick`|`bounce`|`shatter`), `retrievable`, and a `payload` list of property emissions using the e03 vocabulary, e.g. `{applyProperty:"burning", radius:0.3}`, `{applyProperty:"wet", radius:1.5}`, `{spawn:"rope", length:8}`, `{noise:{loudness:70, duration:2}}`, `{impactForceMul:2.5}`. Initial data: standard, broadhead, fire, water, rope, noise, blunt.

## Scope
- In: Schema, validators, initial arrow data file
- Out: Projectile behaviour (e05-arrow-projectile)
- Out: Payload effects (per trick-arrow items)

## Notes
No payload may name a specific target type; validators reject target-specific keys.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the initial arrow file, when validated, then all seven arrows pass and each payload property exists in the e03 world-property vocabulary.
- AC-2 [content] Given a payload referencing an unknown property (e.g. `applyProperty:"sparkly"`), when validated, then it fails with the path.
- AC-3 [content] Given an arrow with negative mass or dragK, when validated, then it fails.
- AC-4 [content] Given a payload key that targets a specific entity type (e.g. `onlyAffects:"rope"`), when validated, then it is rejected as non-systemic.

items.title: Deterministic arrow ballistics with gravity, drag and sticking
items.description:
## Why
Arrows need physical presence — arcs, drop, sticking in wood, glancing off stone — to make archery precise and learnable.

## What
Sim-side projectile integration at 60 Hz: semi-implicit Euler, gravity 9.81 m/s², quadratic drag `a = -k·v·|v| / m`; orientation follows velocity. Each tick a swept segment test runs against hurtboxes (shared e04-hit-volumes query) and world colliders. On hit: damage scales with (v/v0)² clamped to [0.3, 1.0]; stick/penetrate if `penetration` ≥ surface hardness, else ricochet (reflect with 40% speed) or drop. Airborne lifetime 10 s max. Shooter is immune to its own arrow for its first 30 ticks, then can be hit (an arrow shot straight up can come back down).

## Scope
- In: Integration, swept collision, speed-scaled damage, stick/ricochet/drop, lifetime, self-hit rule
- Out: Bow input and draw (e05-bow-core)
- Out: Arrow persistence/pickup (e05-arrow-retrieval)

## Notes
Surface hardness comes from ground/collider material tags (e03-world-properties): soil 5, wood 10, flesh 5, bone 20, stone 40, metal 60.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 60 m/s launch at 30° with k = 0 from ground level, when simulated, then range is within ±1% of the analytic value (≈ 318 m).
- AC-2 [unit] Given drag k from the standard arrow, when simulated, then landing point matches a reference RK4 table within ±0.5 m at 50 m.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an 80 m/s arrow and a 5 cm plank collider, when stepped, then the hit registers (no tunneling).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an arrow with penetration 20 hitting stone (hardness 40), when it hits, then it ricochets at 40% speed and deals no damage.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an arrow shot straight up at 40 m/s, when it falls back through the shooter after 30 ticks, then the shooter is hit; within the first 30 ticks, then not.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a replay of 20 arrows fired at moving dummies, when replayed 100 times, then state hashes are identical every tick.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 60 arrows in flight, when stepped, then projectile update ≤ 0.4 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.

items.title: Bow draw, aim and release firing selected arrow type
items.description:
## Why
Archery must feel excellent from the first shot: a satisfying draw, precise aim and immediate, physical release (Archer fantasy: precision).

## What
As an archer, I want to draw, aim and release arrows so that I can hit precise targets at range.
Hold fire to draw: full draw at 48 ticks (800 ms, shortbow). Launch speed lerps 30%→100% of 60 m/s by draw fraction. Releasing before 12 ticks cancels the shot and returns the arrow. Drawing costs 6 stamina; holding full draw beyond 120 ticks drains 8 stamina/s and at 0 the draw collapses (arrow returned). Aim mode uses the over-shoulder camera from e02-camera (FOV 70→55°), walk speed 50% while drawn. Consumes the selected arrow type from the quiver (e17-inventory-core); a cycle input switches type. Dodge or block cancels the draw and returns the arrow.

## Scope
- In: Draw/release/cancel, launch speed curve, stamina, aim mode hookup, quiver selection, bow data (shortbow)
- Out: Sweet-spot release (e05-draw-timing)
- Out: Sway and reticle (e05-aim-sway)
- Out: Ballistics (e05-arrow-projectile)

## Notes
Anchor e05-bow-core: with e05-arrow-projectile (a dependency) this completes draw, aim, release and arrow physics.
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given draw held for 24 ticks, when released, then an arrow spawns at 65% of full launch speed (30% + 0.5 × 70%).
- AC-2 [unit] Given draw held for 8 ticks, when released, then no arrow spawns and the quiver count is unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given full draw held for 120 ticks, when held further, then stamina drains 8/s and at 0 the draw collapses with the arrow returned.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty quiver for the selected type, when fire is pressed, then the draw does not start and `ActionRejected{reason:"ammo"}` is emitted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a drawn bow, when dodge is pressed, then the draw cancels, the arrow returns to the quiver and the dodge executes.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the archery range in Chromium, when Playwright draws for 48 ticks and releases at the 20 m target, then the target registers a hit and no console errors occur.
- AC-7 [manual] Given a 5-minute archery range session, when three playtesters shoot, then median rating for "the bow feels satisfying" is ≥ 4/5.

items.title: Focused release window and rhythm bonus for well-timed shots
items.description:
## Why
Draw timing gives archery a mastery curve comparable to the knight's parry (Archer fantasy: draw timing).

## What
As an archer, I want a brief sweet spot at full draw so that well-timed releases are rewarded.
**Focused release**: releasing within 6 ticks (100 ms) after reaching full draw → +25% damage, +15% launch speed, zero sway, `FocusedShot` event (reticle pulse + chime cue). **Rhythm**: consecutive focused releases reduce nock time from 20 to 14 ticks, stacking up to 3 times; any unfocused shot or 3 s idle resets stacks.

## Scope
- In: Focused window, bonuses, rhythm stacks, events for presentation
- Out: Reticle visuals (e05-aim-sway)
- Out: Audio chime (e28-bow-audio)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given full draw reached on tick 48, when released on tick 48 or tick 53, then the shot is focused; on tick 47 or tick 54, then it is not.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a focused release, when the arrow spawns, then its damage template is ×1.25 and launch speed ×1.15.
- AC-3 [unit] Given three consecutive focused shots, when the fourth arrow is nocked, then nock time is 14 ticks; after one unfocused shot, then it returns to 20.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 2 rhythm stacks and 3 s without firing, when the next draw starts, then stacks are 0.
- AC-5 [manual] Given the archery range, when three playtesters shoot for 5 minutes, then each can hit the focused window on ≥ 50% of shots by the end and describes it as "satisfying".

items.title: Deterministic aim sway, breath hold and bow reticle
items.description:
## Why
Sway and breath control make long shots a skill and keep the arrow honest to what the reticle shows.

## What
As an archer, I want my aim to steady or waver based on what I am doing so that long shots demand composure.
Sway is simulated (seeded from sim RNG, so replays match): 0° for the first 60 ticks at full draw, then grows 0.1°/s up to 1.5°; walking adds 0.6°; being hit adds a 2° kick decaying over 300 ms; crouched & stationary ("braced") −40%. Hold-breath input at full draw zeroes sway for up to 3 s at 10 stamina/s. Launch direction = reticle direction + current sway offset. Reticle HUD shows draw progress and sway; optional trajectory arc preview (assist, off by default) via settings.

## Scope
- In: Sway model, breath hold, braced modifier, reticle HUD, arc preview assist
- Out: Camera aim mode (e02-camera)
- Out: Lead indicator (e05-moving-targets)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given full draw held for 60 ticks while stationary, when released, then sway offset is exactly 0°.
- AC-2 [unit] Given full draw held 20 s, when sampled, then sway amplitude is capped at 1.5° (0.9° while braced).
- AC-3 [unit] Given breath hold active with 25 stamina, when 3 s pass, then sway stays 0 for 2.5 s and resumes when stamina hits 0.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the same seed and inputs, when two runs fire 10 swaying shots, then launch directions match bit-for-bit.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the arc preview assist disabled (default), when drawing, then no arc renders; enabled, then the arc matches e05-arrow-projectile's prediction within 0.2 m at 30 m.

items.title: Headshots, weak points and armored regions that deflect
items.description:
## Why
"Weak points matter" — precise shots on heads and exposed cores should change fights, and armor should be something you shoot around (Archer fantasy; creature weaknesses).

## What
As an archer, I want headshots and weak points to matter and armor to deflect weak arrows so that where I hit is as important as whether I hit.
Hurtbox regions from e12-creature-schema: `head` ×2.0 (most humanoids), `weakpoint` ×3.0 with ×2 poise damage (can be enabled/disabled by creature state, e.g. a core exposed only while roaring), `armored` regions with an armor value: arrows with penetration < armor ricochet (no damage), blunt arrows ignore deflection but deal ×0.5. A headshot on an unaware humanoid causes an instant stagger. HUD hit markers distinguish normal / headshot / weak point / deflected. Melee uses the same regions.

## Scope
- In: Region multipliers in the damage pipeline, state-toggled weak points, deflection rule, unaware headshot stagger, hit-marker events
- Out: Creature region authoring (e12/e13)
- Out: Stealth unaware state (e11-alert-states — read only)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a humanoid with head ×2.0, when a 20-pierce arrow hits the head, then 40 damage applies and the hit is tagged `headshot`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a weakpoint currently disabled, when an arrow hits its hurtbox, then it resolves against the underlying region instead.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an `armored` region with armor 30 and an arrow with penetration 20, when it hits, then it deflects with 0 damage and a `Deflected` event; a blunt arrow deals ×0.5 instead.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unaware humanoid, when hit in the head, then it staggers regardless of poise.
- AC-5 [content] Given creature data, when validated, then every creature with a `weakpoint` region declares the state(s) in which it is enabled.

items.title: Stuck arrows persist and can be retrieved or looted
items.description:
## Why
Arrows with physical presence that you walk over and pull from a door make the world feel real and keep ammo pressure fair.

## What
As an archer, I want to pull my arrows back out of walls and fallen enemies so that ammo feels physical and I am not punished for practising.
Stuck arrows persist as world entities (cap 64 per area; oldest non-visible despawn first). Interact (e02-interaction) near stuck arrows collects all intact arrows within 1.0 m. Intact chance decided at impact with sim RNG: soil/wood/flesh 90%, stone 40%, metal 20%, burned (fire arrow or burning target) 0% — broken arrows render as broken. Arrows in creatures move with them and drop into their loot on death. Arrows stuck in moving physics objects move with them. Spent trick arrows return as standard arrows if intact.

## Scope
- In: Persistence, cap/despawn policy, pickup, intact roll at impact, corpse loot transfer
- Out: Inventory UI (e17)
- Out: Save of stuck arrows beyond the current area (not persisted)

## Notes
Rope arrows are retrieved only at their anchor and return as rope arrows.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an arrow hitting wood with the seeded RNG roll 0.5, when resolved, then it is intact (0.5 < 0.9) and `retrievable` is true.
- AC-2 [integration] Given three intact arrows stuck within 1.0 m, when the player interacts, then quiver count increases by 3 and the entities are removed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 65 stuck arrows in an area, when the 65th sticks, then the oldest arrow not in view is despawned.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a creature with 2 arrows in it, when it dies, then its loot contains those arrows that were intact.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an arrow stuck in a target that later ignites, when the fire reaches it, then it becomes broken and non-retrievable.

items.title: Fire arrows ignite flammable things; dip arrows in open flame
items.description:
## Why
Setting a distant oil slick or rope alight is a classic archer "wait, I can do that?" — and must emerge from properties, not scripts.

## What
As an archer, I want fire arrows and the ability to light any arrow in a flame so that I can ignite things at range.
Fire arrows carry the `burning` property in flight; on impact they apply `burning` in a 0.3 m radius through e03-element-propagation — any `flammable` object or creature there reacts per its own rules. **Dip to light**: while drawing, if the arrow tip is within 0.8 m of any `burning` entity for 30 ticks, the nocked arrow becomes burning. Burning arrows passing through a water volume or heavy rain are extinguished.

## Scope
- In: Fire payload behaviour, dip-to-light rule, extinguish in water
- Out: Fire spread rules (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: Fire visuals (e29-arrow-fx)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any `flammable` object, when a burning arrow impacts within 0.3 m, then the object gains `burning` via element propagation on that tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a non-flammable stone wall, when a burning arrow impacts, then nothing ignites and the arrow burns out after 3 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a drawn standard arrow held 0.6 m from a burning brazier for 30 ticks, when released, then the arrow carries `burning`; at 29 ticks, then it does not.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a burning arrow that passes through a water volume, when it exits, then it no longer carries `burning` and ignites nothing on impact.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a greybox room with a brazier and an oil-soaked rope bridge, when three fresh archer playtesters play, then at least one discovers dip-to-light unprompted within 5 minutes.

items.title: Water arrows douse fires, extinguish lights and wet surfaces
items.description:
## Why
Dousing a torch from the shadows serves stealth, puzzles and fire-fighting through one property (multiple solutions).

## What
As an archer, I want water arrows that shatter into a splash so that I can put out fires and lights and make surfaces wet.
On impact the arrow shatters and applies `wet` in a 1.5 m radius and removes `burning` from anything inside it (torches, braziers, burning creatures). Extinguished light sources lower the local light level via e03-light-field. Wet surfaces then behave per element rules (e.g. conduct shock). Hitting extreme heat produces whatever e03 rules dictate (e.g. steam). Water arrows never stick.

## Scope
- In: Water payload, extinguish, wet application
- Out: Light-level recomputation (e03-light-field)
- Out: Steam/conduction rules (e03-element-propagation)

## Notes
Related: stealth group — dousing lights increases thief/archer concealment.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any `burning` entity within 1.5 m of impact, when the water arrow shatters, then `burning` is removed from it that tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a lit torch providing light, when extinguished by a water arrow, then the light level queried at the torch's position decreases.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a wet floor and a shock source per e03 rules, when shock is applied, then conduction occurs across the wetted area (property-based, not arrow-specific).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a water arrow, when it hits anything, then it never sticks and is not retrievable.

items.title: Rope arrows anchor into wood and create climbable ropes
items.description:
## Why
Opening a vertical route with a rope arrow is the archer's answer to the locked tower (Classes change possibilities).

## What
As an archer, I want to shoot a rope arrow into a wooden beam and climb it so that I can reach places others cannot.
Rope arrows stick only into surfaces tagged `wood` (or `soft_anchor`) whose normal is within 60° of horizontal or facing downward (beams, ceilings). On stone/metal they bounce off with sparks (readable hint). A hit spawns an 8 m rope entity hanging from the anchor, climbable via e02-player-controller climb hooks. Ropes are `flammable` (burning rope falls and drops climbers) and `cuttable`. Max 3 active ropes per area (oldest retracts).

## Scope
- In: Anchor rule, rope spawn, climb hookup, rope properties, active cap, retrieval at anchor
- Out: Climbing mechanics (e02-player-controller)
- Out: Rope visuals (e29-arrow-fx)

## Notes
Ropes persist while the area is loaded; persistence across saves is not required for MVP.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a wooden beam overhead, when a rope arrow hits it, then an 8 m rope spawns and the player can climb to the beam.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a stone wall, when a rope arrow hits it, then it bounces, no rope spawns and the arrow remains retrievable.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a player climbing a rope, when the rope gains `burning`, then within 3 s it detaches and the player falls (environment fall rules apply).
- AC-4 [unit] Given 3 active ropes, when a 4th is created, then the oldest retracts and returns a rope arrow at its anchor position.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a wooden surface whose normal points 80° upward (a floor), when a rope arrow hits it, then no rope spawns.

items.title: Noise arrows create sound events that lure creatures
items.description:
## Why
Luring a guard away with a rattling arrow is a clean, systemic distraction shared with the stealth model.

## What
As an archer, I want a noise arrow that rattles where it lands so that I can pull creatures toward a spot.
On impact it emits a noise event (loudness 70, duration 2 s) into e09-sound-propagation at the impact point; how creatures react is entirely their perception/AI. In water the loudness is ×0.3. Deals no damage (blunt head, 1 blunt).

## Scope
- In: Noise payload emission, water muffling, positional cue event
- Out: Noise propagation and creature reaction (stealth group)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a noise arrow impact, when resolved, then exactly one noise event of loudness 70 lasting 120 ticks is emitted at the impact position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given impact inside a water volume, when resolved, then the noise event loudness is 21.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature within hearing range per e09 rules, when the noise event propagates, then the creature receives it (reaction owned by AI; test asserts delivery only).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a noise arrow hitting a creature, when resolved, then it deals ≤ 1 damage and causes no reaction beyond flinch rules.

items.title: Blunt arrows knock objects, press switches and stun
items.description:
## Why
Non-lethal, physics-first arrows let the archer solve problems by shoving the world rather than killing it.

## What
As an archer, I want blunt arrows that hit hard without sticking so that I can knock things over, press switches at range and stun unaware foes.
Blunt damage, penetration 0, poise damage ×2.5, `impactForceMul` 2.5, never sticks (drops at impact; always retrievable unless it lands in a hazard). Applies impulse to physics objects (knock a bucket off a shelf). A head hit on an unaware creature whose schema allows `knockout` renders it unconscious for 60 s (non-lethal).

## Scope
- In: Blunt behaviour, impulse, knockout rule
- Out: Switch/mechanism triggering (e05-shoot-mechanisms)
- Out: Unconscious state handling in AI (e11)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a 3 kg object on a shelf, when hit by a blunt arrow, then it receives an impulse and falls.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an unaware creature with `knockout: true`, when hit in the head by a blunt arrow, then it becomes unconscious for 3600 ticks.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an aware creature, when hit in the head by a blunt arrow, then it is not knocked out and takes blunt damage with ×2.5 poise damage.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a blunt arrow impact on any surface, when resolved, then it does not stick and is retrievable at the impact point.

items.title: Shootable triggers and cuttable ropes activate mechanisms
items.description:
## Why
"The archer might shoot a distant mechanism." Shooting targets, bells and ropes opens routes at range (Classes change possibilities; puzzle constitution).

## What
As an archer, I want to shoot distant targets and ropes so that I can open gates, drop chandeliers and trigger mechanisms from afar.
Objects with the `shootable` property fire an e03 switch signal when any projectile hits with impulse ≥ their threshold. Objects with `cuttable` (ropes, cords) are severed by pierce/slash damage landing on them; anything they suspend becomes a free physics object. Fully property-driven: thrown daggers or spell projectiles that produce the same packet also work.

## Scope
- In: Shootable signal emission, cuttable severing, examples in the archery range
- Out: Mechanism wiring (e03-doors-locks-switches)
- Out: Level placement (e26 dungeon)

## Notes
Related: puzzle group (e15-puzzle-kit) consumes shootable/cuttable in puzzle designs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a `shootable` target wired to a gate, when an arrow hits it with impulse ≥ threshold, then the gate receives the switch signal and opens.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a chandelier hanging from a `cuttable` rope, when a broadhead arrow hits the rope, then the rope severs and the chandelier falls as a physics object.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the same rope, when a blunt arrow hits it, then it does not sever (blunt only).
