- AC-4 [unit] Given a `shootable` target, when a projectile hits below threshold impulse, then no signal is emitted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a non-arrow projectile producing a pierce packet, when it hits a `cuttable` rope, then the rope severs identically.

items.title: Greybox archery range for tuning and e2e tests
items.description:
## Why
Draw timing, drop and trick arrows need a fast, repeatable test space just as melee has the combat sandbox.

## What
As a developer, I want an archery range scene so that I can tune ballistics and verify trick arrows quickly.
Static targets at 10/20/40/60 m, targets on rails at 2/4/6 m/s, a 6 m elevated platform, an overhead wooden beam (rope anchor), a brazier, a `shootable` bell wired to a door, a `cuttable` rope holding a crate, a pool of water. Stats overlay: hit %, flight time, impact speed, focused-shot rate.

## Scope
- In: Scene, fixtures, stats overlay, deterministic seed
- Out: Final art for the range (none planned)

## Notes
Lives alongside the combat sandbox under /dev/archery.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the range loaded in Chromium, when it boots, then all fixtures exist, no console errors occur and the overlay reads 0 shots.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the rail targets, when 10 s elapse, then their positions match the deterministic schedule within 0.01 m.
- AC-3 [integration] Given 10 scripted shots at the 20 m target, when complete, then the overlay hit % equals hits/shots from sim events.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the bell/door fixture, when an arrow hits the bell, then the door opens within 1 s.

items.title: Elevation grants archery damage and range advantage
items.description:
## Why
High ground should matter to an archer: climbing a tower should change the fight (Archer fantasy: elevation).

## What
As an archer, I want shooting from above to hit harder and reach farther so that seeking high ground is a real tactic.
Range gain is natural from ballistics. Additionally: shooter at ≥ 3 m above target → +15% damage; ≥ 6 m → +25% (data-tunable). Implemented as an attacker-stage modifier in the damage pipeline tagged `elevation`.

## Scope
- In: Elevation modifier, thresholds in data
- Out: AI reaction to unreachable attackers (e11)

## Notes
Related: AI group should give melee creatures a behaviour for unreachable archers (seek path, throw rocks, take cover).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a shooter 4 m above the target, when a 20-pierce arrow hits, then 23 damage applies and the hit is tagged `elevation`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a shooter 2.9 m above, when an arrow hits, then no elevation bonus applies.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a 30%-draw shot from 10 m height versus ground level, when simulated, then horizontal range increases by ≥ 20%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a shooter below the target, when an arrow hits, then no bonus or penalty applies.

items.title: Moving-target payoffs: leg stumbles, wing downs, lead assist
items.description:
## Why
Hitting a running target should be hard and rewarding (Archer fantasy: moving targets).

## What
As an archer, I want well-led shots on moving creatures to trip or ground them so that tracking a target is worth mastering.
A `limb` (leg) hit on a creature moving > 3 m/s causes a stumble (60-tick knockdown for bipeds; quadrupeds slowed 50% for 3 s). A `wing` region hit on a flying creature grounds it for 4 s. Optional lead-indicator assist (off by default): shows the intercept point for the lock-on target from its velocity and arrow flight time (3-iteration solver).

## Scope
- In: Moving-limb stumble rule, wing grounding, lead solver + indicator assist
- Out: Flying locomotion (e12)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a biped moving at 4 m/s, when a leg region is hit, then it is knocked down for 60 ticks; moving at 2 m/s, then normal hit reactions apply.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a flying creature, when its wing region is hit, then it is grounded for 240 ticks.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target moving at a constant 5 m/s at 30 m, when the lead solver runs, then its predicted intercept is within 0.3 m of the simulated arrow impact.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the lead assist disabled (default), when locked on, then no indicator renders.

items.title: Archer mobility: quickstep while drawn and aerial shots
items.description:
## Why
The archer's fantasy is precision **and** movement; they should reposition without losing a draw.

## What
As an archer, I want to sidestep while holding a draw and shoot mid-jump so that I can stay mobile under pressure.
Quickstep: 12-tick sidestep with i-frames ticks 2–7, 15 stamina, retains up to 60% of current draw. Aerial shot: firing while airborne is allowed with +1.0° additional spread; draw progress continues in the air.

## Scope
- In: Quickstep move, draw retention, aerial shot spread
- Out: Knight roll (e04-dodge-iframes)

## Notes
Timing convention: sim runs at a fixed 60 Hz (1 tick = 16.67 ms, per e00-sim-core). All frame numbers are sim ticks; ms values are for readability only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given full draw, when quickstep executes, then draw fraction after it is 0.6 and i-frames cover ticks 2–7.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 40% draw, when quickstep executes, then draw fraction remains 0.4 (retention caps at 60%, never increases).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player airborne, when an arrow is released, then its spread includes +1.0°.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the range with rail targets, when three playtesters use quickstep, then median rating for "I feel mobile as an archer" is ≥ 4/5.

items.title: Extended trick arrows as pure data: frost, shock, smoke
items.description:
## Why
Proves the systemic promise: new arrows need data, not code, and immediately interact with existing world properties.

## What
As a designer, I want to add frost, shock and smoke arrows purely in data so that the arrow roster grows without engineering.
Frost applies `frozen` (e.g. water surfaces become walkable ice per e03 rules); shock applies `electrified` (conducts through wet/conductive); smoke spawns a vision-blocking volume. No new sim code beyond what payload types already support.

## Scope
- In: Three arrow data entries, tests exercising each
- Out: New payload primitives (would need a separate engineering bead)

## Notes
If any arrow needs code, split that capability into its own bead first.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three new arrow entries, when validated, then they pass with no schema changes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a water surface, when a frost arrow impacts it, then it gains `frozen` per e03 rules.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a smoke arrow impact, when resolved, then a vision-blocking volume exists for its declared duration and blocks sight queries through it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the change set for this bead, when reviewed, then no files under src/sim are modified (asserted by a CI path check on the PR).

items.title: Web Audio engine: registry, buses, voice pool, positional audio
items.description:
## Why
Every weapon, footstep and creature needs a robust, browser-safe audio core before feedback can feel satisfying (E28 outcome).

## What
A `src/audio` engine: lazily created `AudioContext`, resumed on first user gesture (autoplay policy) with a queue that plays requests younger than 2 s and drops older ones. Sound registry from a content manifest (id → url(s), variants, bus, spatial, loop, priority). Decode + LRU cache (cap 64 MB decoded). Bus graph: master → music, sfx (subgroups combat, footsteps, creatures), ambience, ui. Positional audio via `PannerNode` (HRTF on High, equalpower on Low), inverse distance, ref 2 m, max 40 m. Listener follows the camera each render frame. Voice pool max 48 (Low 24) with priority + distance stealing. API: `play(cueId, {position|entity, volume, pitch}) → handle` with stop/fade.

## Scope
- In: Context lifecycle, registry, cache, buses, panner, listener, voice pool, handle API
- In: Fake AudioContext test double for ≥ 90% coverage of src/audio
- Out: Mapping sim events to sounds (e28-cue-sheets)
- Out: Volume settings UI (e28-mixer-settings)
- Out: Sound asset creation (art/audio group)

## Notes
Presentation only: nothing in src/audio may write to sim state. Related: stealth noise simulation is owned by e09-sound-propagation.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a suspended AudioContext, when `play` is called before any gesture, then the request is queued; on resume, requests younger than 2 s play and older ones are dropped.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 48 active voices, when a higher-priority request arrives, then the lowest-priority, farthest voice is stolen; when a lower-priority request arrives, then it is rejected.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sound attached to a moving entity, when the entity moves, then the panner position updates in the same frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unknown cue id, when played, then a null handle is returned, one warning is logged per id, and nothing throws.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a corrupt audio file, when decoding fails, then the id is marked failed and dev builds substitute a placeholder beep; production stays silent.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, when the page is clicked and a test cue plays, then `AudioContext.state` is `running` and no console errors occur.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 48 positional voices on moving entities, when measured, then main-thread audio update ≤ 0.5 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine.

items.title: Placeholder sound pack keyed by final asset ids
items.description:
## Why
Gameplay is never blocked by final audio; placeholders named with final ids make swapping in real assets a file replacement.

## What
A script (`tools/audio/gen-placeholders`) synthesising simple placeholder sounds (filtered noise bursts, tones, clicks) or pulling CC0 clips, written under the final asset ids (e.g. `sfx-knight-parry-metal-01`). Manifest entries flagged `placeholder: true`. A dev report lists remaining placeholders so the asset group can prioritise prompt beads.

## Scope
- In: Generator script, initial placeholder set for combat/archery/footsteps/UI, manifest flags, placeholder report
- Out: Final SFX creation (art/audio group, e38)

## Notes
Initial ids are listed in the combat plan summary for the asset group. Licences for any CC0 clips go in assets/CREDITS.md.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given all cue sheets, when validated, then every referenced sound id resolves to a manifest entry (placeholder or final).
- AC-2 [content] Given the placeholder set, when measured, then total size ≤ 2 MB.
- AC-3 [content] Given any CC0-sourced placeholder, when validated, then it has a licence/provenance line in assets/CREDITS.md.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the placeholder report command, when run, then it lists every id with `placeholder: true` and a total count.

items.title: Data-driven cue sheets map sim events to sounds
items.description:
## Why
Sounds must follow game events without hard-coded calls scattered across code, and must never influence the deterministic sim.

## What
A game-layer bridge subscribing to sim events and resolving **cue sheet** rules (content data): `{event, match:{...tags}, cue, variants, pitchJitter, volumeJitterDb, cooldownMs, priority}`. Most-specific match wins. A separate presentation RNG handles variation (never the sim RNG). Identical cues on the same entity within 30 ms are de-duplicated. The rule matcher is generic so e29-vfx-cue-sheets reuses it.

## Scope
- In: Rule schema, matcher, bridge, presentation RNG, de-dupe, initial rules for combat events
- Out: Specific sound sets (per-feature audio items)

## Notes
Put the matcher in src/game/cues so VFX shares it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given rules for `DamageApplied` generic and `DamageApplied{weapon:"metal", target:"bone"}`, when a metal-on-bone hit occurs, then the specific cue plays.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two identical cue requests on one entity 20 ms apart, when processed, then only one plays.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 60 s combat replay run with audio enabled and disabled, when compared, then sim state hashes are identical every tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rule with 4 variants and pitch jitter ±5%, when triggered 1000 times, then all variants occur and pitch stays within ±5%.
- AC-5 [content] Given a cue sheet referencing an unknown sim event type, when validated, then it fails with the rule index.

items.title: Combat impact audio matrix: hits, blocks, parries, whiffs
items.description:
## Why
Sound carries half of combat weight; a parry must ring out and a heavy blow must thud (Combat is intrinsically fun).

## What
As a knight, I want every hit, block and parry to sound distinct so that I can read the fight by ear.
Impact matrix: attacker material (blade, blunt-wood, blunt-metal, claw, bone, arrow) × target material (flesh, bone, metal armor, wood shield, metal shield, stone, wood) → cue. Distinct high-priority cues for block, parry (never stolen), guard break, riposte, wall recoil; whooshes by weapon class and light/heavy; stamina-rejected wheeze; charge-ready. Impact cues start on the first hit-stop frame; volume tier by light/heavy/critical.

## Scope
- In: Cue sheet rules, material tags on moves/hurtboxes, parry priority, hit-stop sync
- Out: Final SFX (asset group)
- Out: Creature vocals (e28-creature-audio-hooks)

## Notes
Uses placeholders from e28-placeholder-sounds until final assets integrate.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sword hitting a skeleton (bone), when `DamageApplied` fires, then the blade×bone cue plays at the victim position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a successful parry during a 48-voice saturation test, when it fires, then the parry cue plays (not stolen) and a lower-priority voice is dropped.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a heavy hit with 5-tick hit-stop, when it lands, then the impact cue starts within the first frozen frame (≤ 17 ms after the event).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a material pair without a specific rule, when resolved, then the attacker-material generic cue plays (no silence).
- AC-5 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters close their eyes during a dummy fight, then each can distinguish block, parry and clean hit by sound alone.

items.title: Per-bus volume settings, tab-hidden mute and mono option
items.description:
## Why
Players must control their mix; accessibility options such as mono downmix matter for hearing-impaired players (E31).

## What
As a player, I want volume sliders per category and audio accessibility options so that I can hear the game the way I need.
Sliders for master, music, sfx, ambience, ui (0–100 mapped to a perceptual −60..0 dB curve, 0 = mute); mute when tab hidden (default on); mono downmix; "night mode" dynamic range compressor. Persisted through e31-settings-framework, applied with a 50 ms ramp (no clicks).

## Scope
- In: Bus gain control, settings entries, persistence, ramps, mono and compressor options
- Out: Mix snapshots/ducking (e28-mix-snapshots)
- Out: Sound captions (e28-sound-captions)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given sfx slider set to 50, when applied, then the sfx bus gain equals the curve value for 50 and ramps over 50 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given slider 0, when applied, then the bus gain is exactly 0.
- AC-3 [integration] Given tab-hidden mute on, when `visibilitychange` reports hidden, then master ramps to 0; on visible, it restores the previous value.
- AC-4 [integration] Given settings changed and the page reloaded, when the audio engine boots, then saved bus volumes are applied before the first sound plays.
- AC-5 [unit] Given mono downmix on, when a hard-left panned source plays, then both output channels carry equal signal.

items.title: Surface-aware footsteps modulated by stance and armor
items.description:
## Why
Footsteps ground the character in the world and teach players how loud they are — the audible face of the stealth system.

## What
As a player, I want footsteps that change with the surface, my stance and my armor so that I can hear where and how I am moving.
Foot plant events from animation, with a stride-distance fallback (every 0.7 m walking, 1.1 m running). Surface from the ground collider material tag (stone, wood, dirt, grass, shallow-water, metal, rug, gravel). Crouch −10 dB, sprint +3 dB; armor layer (chain jingle / plate clank) by e04-armor-weight class; landing sounds scale with fall height. Creatures use the same system with their own sets.

## Scope
- In: Foot plant bridge, surface lookup, stance/armor modulation, landings, creature reuse
- Out: Sim noise emission for stealth (e09-sound-propagation) — audio reads the same surface table but never emits sim noise

## Notes
Shared read-only surface table keeps audible loudness consistent with stealth noise values.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player walking from stone onto wood, when the next foot plant occurs, then a wood footstep variant plays.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a crouched player, when a footstep cue resolves, then its volume is 10 dB below the standing value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no animation foot plant events (fallback mode), when the player walks 3.5 m, then exactly 5 footsteps play.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unknown surface tag, when resolved, then the stone set plays and a dev warning names the tag once.
- AC-5 [integration] Given plate armor, when walking, then each footstep also plays the plate layer.

items.title: Bow audio: draw creak, release, flyby and payload cues
items.description:
## Why
A creaking draw and a sharp release make the bow feel tense and powerful (Archery epic outcome: bows feel excellent).

## What
As an archer, I want the bow to creak as I draw and arrows to whistle past so that shots feel tense and physical.
Draw creak loop whose playbackRate (0.9→1.1) and gain follow draw fraction; focused-release chime; release twang by draw strength; arrow flyby when passing within 3 m of the listener (pitch bend simulating doppler); impacts reuse the combat material matrix; ricochet; trick payload cues (ignite, splash, rope unfurl, rattle); pickup cue on retrieval.

## Scope
- In: Continuous draw loop control, flyby detection, cue rules for bow events
- Out: Final bow SFX (asset group)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given draw fraction 0.5, when the creak loop updates, then playbackRate is 1.0 and gain is the 50% curve value.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an arrow passing 2 m from the listener, when its closest approach occurs, then one flyby cue plays; at 4 m, then none.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a focused release event, when processed, then the chime plays in the same frame as the release twang.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the draw is cancelled, when processed, then the creak loop fades out within 100 ms and no release twang plays.

items.title: Creature audio slots and audible attack telegraphs
items.description:
## Why
Creatures feel alive through sound, and an audible telegraph before a big attack is key to Zelda-like readability.

## What
As a player, I want creatures to sound distinct and warn me audibly before big attacks so that I can react without staring at them.
Creature schema audio slots: idle loop, footstep set, alert bark, attack telegraph, hurt, poise break, death. Telegraph cues play on `TelegraphStarted` and must start ≥ 250 ms before active frames; unblockable moves use a distinct high-priority telegraph. Alert-state transitions (Suspicious, Alerted, Combat) expose hook events for stingers.

## Scope
- In: Schema audio slots, telegraph cue playback, alert-state hook events
- Out: Creature sound creation (asset group)
- Out: Alert-state logic (e11-alert-states)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given creature data, when validated, then every creature declares all required audio slots (placeholder ids allowed).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a skeleton starting an unblockable move, when `TelegraphStarted` fires, then the unblockable telegraph cue plays ≥ 250 ms before the move's first active tick.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature transitioning Suspicious→Alerted, when the event fires, then the alert bark plays at its position and a `MusicStinger` hook event is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature dies while its idle loop plays, when `Died` is processed, then the loop stops within 200 ms and the death cue plays.

items.title: Mix snapshots and ducking for combat, stealth and menus
items.description:
## Why
The mix should focus attention: a parry should cut through the music, and a pause menu should feel like a breath.

## What
As a player, I want the mix to shift with the situation so that important sounds cut through when they matter.
Snapshots (explore, stealth, combat, menu, paused) define bus gains and filters (paused = low-pass 800 Hz on sfx/ambience). Transitions ramp 250–1500 ms. Ducking: music and ambience duck −6 dB for 400 ms on parry/critical; sfx ducks −4 dB under UI stingers. Snapshot selection follows game state (alert state via e11-alert-states, pause menu).

## Scope
- In: Snapshot data, transition ramps, ducking rules, state bindings
- Out: Adaptive music layers (e28-adaptive-music)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the explore snapshot, when the game enters Combat alert state, then bus gains ramp to combat values over the configured duration.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a parry event, when processed, then music and ambience are −6 dB for 400 ms and restore with a 200 ms ramp.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the pause menu opens, when the snapshot applies, then sfx/ambience are low-passed at 800 Hz and restore on close.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two overlapping duck requests, when processed, then attenuation takes the deepest value, not the sum.

items.title: Audio occlusion through walls and doors
items.description:
## Why
Hearing a muffled fight behind a door is atmosphere and information; it should match how creatures hear (the stealth model) conceptually.

## What
As a player, I want sounds behind walls and doors to be muffled so that I can judge where things are and whether a door is open.
For the top 16 priority sources within 30 m, raycast listener↔source at 10 Hz (staggered). Occluded: low-pass 22 kHz→900 Hz and −8 dB; closed door on the path: −12 dB and 600 Hz; open door: unoccluded path. 150 ms smoothing. Door states from e03-doors-locks-switches; acoustic values shared with the stealth group's door constants.

## Scope
- In: Ray scheduling, filter/gain mapping, door state lookup, smoothing
- Out: Sim noise occlusion for creatures (e09-sound-propagation)
- Out: Full path-finding propagation (post-MVP)

## Notes
Budget: ≤ 16 rays per 100 ms.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a source behind a solid wall, when occlusion updates, then its low-pass cutoff settles at 900 Hz and gain at −8 dB within 150 ms.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a source behind a closed door that then opens, when occlusion updates, then filtering clears within 150 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 40 eligible sources, when scheduled, then only the 16 highest-priority are raycast and no more than 16 rays run per 100 ms.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the listener inside a collider (camera clipping), when raycasting, then the result is treated as unoccluded (no false muffling).

items.title: Adaptive music controller with layered stems and stingers
items.description:
## Why
Music that swells into combat and relaxes afterwards carries mood without despair (tone: warmer souls-like).

## What
As a player, I want the music to follow the tension of the moment so that exploration, stealth and combat each feel distinct.
A music controller playing location tracks as synchronised stems (explore, tension, stealth, combat), cross-fading layers on bar boundaries using BPM metadata (within 2 bars). Combat layer enters on alert state Combat and exits 8 s after no hostile remains in Combat. Stinger hook events (from e28-creature-audio-hooks) play one-shots quantised to the next beat. Music streams via media elements to protect the initial download budget.

## Scope
- In: Stem sync, bar-quantised crossfades, state bindings, stingers, streaming
- Out: Music composition in Suno (asset group, e38)

## Notes
Placeholder stems: simple generated drones/pulses at 90 BPM until Suno tracks integrate.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 90 BPM track and a layer change requested mid-bar, when processed, then the crossfade starts on the next bar boundary (≤ 2.67 s).
- AC-2 [integration] Given combat ends, when 8 s pass with no creature in Combat state, then the combat layer fades out; if combat resumes at 6 s, then it does not.
- AC-3 [integration] Given all four stems playing, when measured after 5 minutes, then stem drift is ≤ 10 ms.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a music track fails to load, when the controller starts, then it continues silently and logs once without affecting sfx.

items.title: Reverb zones per space: caves, halls, interiors, forest
items.description:
## Why
Acoustic space sells the dungeon: a sword clang should echo in the labyrinth and die in the forest.

## What
As a player, I want each space to sound like its size and material so that caves, halls and forests feel different.
Convolution reverb sends per zone type (cave, stone hall, wooden interior, forest, open field) using impulse-response assets; zone chosen via e03-triggers volumes; 1 s crossfade across boundaries; Low preset uses a single shared convolver with fewer IRs.

## Scope
- In: Reverb send buses, zone volumes, crossfade, Low-preset fallback, placeholder IRs
- Out: Recorded/generated IR assets (asset group)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the listener entering a cave trigger volume, when processed, then the cave send ramps to its target over 1 s while the previous zone fades.
- AC-2 [unit] Given overlapping zones, when resolved, then the zone with the highest declared priority wins.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the Low preset, when zones switch, then at most one ConvolverNode exists.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a missing IR asset, when the zone activates, then the dry signal plays unaffected and a warning is logged.

items.title: Ambient beds and randomised positional one-shots
items.description:
## Why
Dripping caves and rustling forests make exploration rewarding even when nothing is fighting you (The world rewards curiosity).

## What
As a player, I want each place to have its own living soundscape so that quiet exploration is atmospheric.
Per-zone ambient bed loops (2 s crossfade) plus randomised positional one-shots (drips, wind gusts, distant birds, creaks) with min/max interval and spawn radius, defined in zone data and placed via e03-triggers.

## Scope
- In: Ambience zone data, bed crossfades, one-shot scheduler
- Out: Ambience assets (asset group)

## Notes

**Integration note:** Promoted to P1 — the MVP ambience beds (town, wilds, dungeon, river, harbour) are P1 and play through this runtime.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a one-shot with interval 4–9 s, when 10 minutes elapse, then every gap falls within [4, 9] s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the listener crossing between two ambience zones, when processed, then beds crossfade over 2 s with no gap in loudness greater than 3 dB.
- AC-3 [unit] Given one-shot spawn radius 10–25 m, when spawned, then each position lies within that annulus around the listener.

items.title: Directional sound captions for important cues
items.description:
## Why
Deaf and hard-of-hearing players need footsteps behind them and attack telegraphs as much as anyone (E31 accessibility).

## What
As a player, I want captions for important sounds with a direction hint so that I do not miss audio-only information.
Cue-sheet rules may flag `caption: <stringId>`; captions show text such as "[Footsteps, behind left]" with a direction arrow relative to the camera, only for sources within 20 m, de-duplicated per source for 2 s, max 4 visible. Toggle and text size via e31-settings-framework.

## Scope
- In: Caption flag in cue data, caption UI, direction computation, settings
- Out: Dialogue subtitles (dialogue group)

## Notes
Initial flagged cues: footsteps (creatures), creature telegraphs, alert barks, noise-arrow rattle, door open/close, breaking objects.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a flagged cue from a source 135° to the camera's left-rear, when captioned, then the direction label is "behind left".
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same source triggering 5 times in 1 s, when captioned, then only one caption shows.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a flagged source 25 m away, when it plays, then no caption appears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 6 simultaneous captions, when rendered, then the 4 highest-priority show.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given captions enabled in settings, when a creature telegraph plays in the sandbox, then the caption appears within 100 ms.

items.title: Audio performance and download budgets
items.description:
## Why
Audio must fit the hardware baseline: ≤ 50 MB initial download and steady 60 fps.

## What
Budgets added to the e32 perf suite: decoded audio memory ≤ 96 MB; main-thread audio work ≤ 0.5 ms/frame p95; voices ≤ 48 High / 24 Low; audio share of initial download ≤ 12 MB (music streamed); format strategy (Opus in WebM/Ogg with AAC fallback for Safari).

## Scope
- In: Budget assertions, format pipeline, lazy-load per area
- Out: Global perf suite (e32-perf-budgets)

## Notes
Cites the contract hardware baseline; no new targets invented beyond audio shares.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the combat stress scene, when profiled on the reference machine, then main-thread audio work ≤ 0.5 ms per frame p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given a cold load of the vertical slice, when measured, then audio bytes before playable ≤ 12 MB.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a 20-minute scripted session, when measured, then decoded audio memory never exceeds 96 MB.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given Safari (WebKit), when sounds load, then the AAC fallback is selected and plays without errors.

items.title: Data-driven VFX framework with pooling and particle budgets
items.description:
## Why
Impacts, magic and destruction establish the visual identity; one budgeted framework keeps spectacle within the performance baseline (E29 outcome).

## What
Renderer-agnostic VFX interface (implemented in src/render/vfx after e00-engine-decision). Effect definitions as content data: emitters (rate/burst, lifetime, velocity cone, size/colour/alpha curves, texture/flipbook id, blend mode), sockets, duration/loop, quality tiers. Instanced particle rendering with pooling (no per-spawn allocations after warm-up). **Budget manager** (pure TS in src/game/vfx, unit-testable): global cap 4000 particles High / 1500 Low, per-effect priority, distance culling at 60 m, LOD tiers. API: `spawn(effectId, {position | entity+socket, rotation, scale, params}) → handle`. Presentation RNG only — never the sim RNG.

## Scope
- In: Effect schema, runtime, pooling, budget manager, socket attachment, debug stats overlay
- Out: Event→effect mapping (e29-vfx-cue-sheets)
- Out: Specific effects (per-feature VFX items)
- Out: Final textures (asset group)

## Notes
Render-specific code is covered by Playwright smoke + perf; budget/pool logic sits in src/game for ≥ 90% unit coverage.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given an effect definition with a negative lifetime or unknown blend mode, when validated, then it fails with the path.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the High cap of 4000 and a request that would exceed it, when evaluated, then lower-priority effects are culled first and the new effect is admitted only if its priority is higher.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a pool warmed to 64 instances of an effect, when 64 spawn and expire repeatedly for 1000 cycles, then no new allocations occur (pool counter unchanged).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an effect 70 m from the camera, when spawned, then it is culled without consuming budget.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an unknown effect id, when spawned, then a null handle returns, dev builds show a magenta marker, and nothing throws.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed in Chromium, when 20 test effects spawn, then they render with no console errors and a screenshot sanity check passes.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 50 simultaneous effects at the High cap, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine.

items.title: Procedural placeholder VFX textures keyed by final asset ids
items.description:
## Why
Effects must be tunable before final art exists; placeholders under final ids make integration a swap.

## What
A tool (`tools/vfx/gen-placeholders`) generating soft circle, spark streak, smoke puff (noise), ring, shard and flame flipbook textures, saved under final asset ids with `placeholder: true` manifest flags, plus a report listing remaining placeholders.

## Scope
- In: Generator, initial texture set, manifest flags, report
- Out: Final VFX textures via GPT image prompts (asset group, e37)

## Notes
Ids listed in the combat plan summary for the asset group.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given all effect definitions, when validated, then every referenced texture id resolves to a manifest entry.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the generator with a fixed seed, when run twice, then outputs are byte-identical.
- AC-3 [content] Given the placeholder set, when measured, then total size ≤ 1.5 MB.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the report command, when run, then it lists all `placeholder: true` textures with a count.

items.title: VFX cue sheets map sim events to effects
items.description:
## Why
Effects should follow events from data, sharing audio's matcher so sound and visuals stay in sync.

## What
A game-layer bridge reusing the generic rule matcher from e28-cue-sheets: `{event, match:{...}, effect, socket, orientTo:"hitNormal"|"attackerForward", scaleBy}`. Effects attached to an entity detach and finish gracefully when it is destroyed (no orphaned loops).

## Scope
- In: VFX rule schema, bridge, attachment lifecycle, initial rules
- Out: Specific effects (per-feature items)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given generic and material-specific rules for `DamageApplied`, when a metal-on-metal hit occurs, then the specific effect spawns oriented to the hit normal.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a looping effect attached to an entity, when the entity is destroyed, then emission stops and existing particles finish within their lifetime.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a 60 s combat replay with VFX on and off, when compared, then sim state hashes are identical every tick.
- AC-4 [content] Given a VFX rule referencing an unknown effect id, when validated, then it warns (placeholder allowed) with the rule index.

items.title: Impact VFX by material: sparks, splinters, bone dust, parry flash
items.description:
## Why
Visible impacts confirm hits instantly and give combat its crunch; the stylised, gore-free look fits the warmer tone.

## What
As a knight, I want every hit to burst with a material-appropriate effect so that I can see what connected and how hard.
Effects: metal sparks, wood splinters, bone chips/dust, stylised ichor puff (no gore), stone chips; block sparks/wood chips; parry flash (radial star + brief bloom boost, never culled); guard-break shatter ring; critical/riposte burst. Enemy hit flash (emissive white 80 ms). Oriented to hit normal, scaled by damage tier.

## Scope
- In: Effect definitions, cue rules, hit flash material param
- Out: Final textures (asset group)
- Out: Screen shake (e29-screen-feedback)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sword hitting a metal-armored target, when `DamageApplied` fires, then the metal-sparks effect spawns at the contact point oriented to the hit normal.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a parry at the particle cap, when it fires, then the parry flash still spawns (priority highest) and lower-priority particles are culled.
- AC-3 [integration] Given any damaged creature, when hit, then its emissive flash lasts 80 ms ± one frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a material pair with no specific rule, when resolved, then a generic impact puff spawns (never nothing).
- AC-5 [manual] Given the sandbox, when three playtesters fight, then each can say which hits were blocked versus clean from visuals alone.

items.title: Camera shake, damage vignette and low-health effects
items.description:
## Why
Screen feedback sells impact and danger, but must respect motion sensitivity and photosensitivity.

## What
As a player, I want the camera to react to big impacts and the screen to warn me when I am hurt so that danger is felt — and I want to turn it down if it bothers me.
Trauma-based shake (trauma 0–1, offset ∝ trauma², decay 1.5/s; light hit 0.15, heavy 0.3, guard break 0.5, explosions distance-scaled). Shake scale slider 0–100% and reduce-motion toggle via e31-settings-framework. Damage vignette for 300 ms scaled by % health lost; desaturation below 25% health. No full-screen flash more than 3 times per second (WCAG 2.3.1).

## Scope
- In: Shake model, vignette, low-health grade, settings hooks, flash limiter
- Out: Camera rig itself (e02-camera)
- Out: Hit-stop timing (e04-hit-stop)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given trauma 0.3 added, when 200 ms pass with no new trauma, then trauma is 0.0 (0.3 − 1.5 × 0.2).
- AC-2 [unit] Given shake scale 0% or reduce-motion on, when trauma is added, then camera offset is exactly 0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 5 flash requests within 1 s, when processed, then at most 3 full-screen flashes render.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a hit removing 40% of health, when processed, then vignette intensity is 0.4 of max and fades by 300 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given A/B shake settings, when three playtesters fight for 3 minutes, then none report nausea at the default and all rate impact ≥ 4/5.

items.title: Weapon swing trails and charge build-up glow
items.description:
## Why
Trails make arcs and reach readable — useful for learning timing — and add spectacle to heavy blows.

## What
As a knight, I want to see the arc of my swings and my charge building so that reach and timing are readable.
Ribbon trails from weapon sockets rendered only during active frames (from sim phase), tinted by dominant damage type; charge build-up glow stepping at 33/66/100% charge with a burst on `ChargeReady`; faint trails on focused arrows. Socket samples smoothed with Catmull-Rom; max 8 concurrent trails.

## Scope
- In: Trail renderer, phase binding, tint mapping, charge glow
- Out: Weapon models (art)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a light attack, when it runs, then the trail is visible only on frames whose sim tick lies in the active window.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a fire-damage weapon, when swung, then the trail uses the fire tint from data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 9 trail requests, when processed, then the oldest trail is released and 8 remain.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a charged heavy reaching full charge, when `ChargeReady` fires, then the burst effect spawns at the weapon socket.

items.title: Magical material library: dissolve, glow, distortion, runes
items.description:
## Why
"Magic should feel magical." A shared shader library gives spells, summons and deaths a consistent, spectacular look.

## What
As a designer, I want a library of magical materials so that spells, summons and deaths share a spectacular, consistent look.
Reusable materials/shaders: dissolve (death, summon, illusion fade), fresnel glow, heat-haze/distortion (High only; Low falls back to none), rune decal projection, emissive pulse, soft particles with depth fade. Parameterised for tint and intensity. Creature death uses dissolve by default (skeletons collapse then dissolve).

## Scope
- In: Shader/material set, parameters, Low-preset fallbacks, creature death dissolve
- Out: Spell-specific art (sorcerer/asset groups)

## Notes
Renderer-specific; covered by Playwright screenshot sanity + perf.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a material test scene, when each shader renders, then screenshot sanity checks pass and no shader compile errors are logged in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Low preset, when distortion is requested, then it is skipped and no distortion pass runs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature `Died` event, when processed, then the dissolve runs over 1.2 s and the render entity is removed afterwards.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 6 simultaneous distortion effects on High, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine.

items.title: Visuals derived from element states: burning, wet, frozen, shock
items.description:
## Why
Systemic visuals mean any object that catches fire looks on fire without per-object authoring — the visual half of the property engine.

## What
As a player, I want anything burning, wet, frozen or electrified to look it so that I can read the world's state at a glance.
The VFX layer observes e03 element states on any entity: `burning` → flame emitter scaled to bounds + smoke; `wet` → darkened material + drips; `frozen` → frost shader + ice crust; `electrified` → arcs; transitions (e.g. burning→wet) → steam puff; gas volumes → tinted fog. Pure presentation — states come from the sim.

## Scope
- In: State observers, bounds-scaled emitters, material parameter blending, transition effects
- Out: Element rules (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: Light emission from fire (e03-light-field)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any entity gaining `burning`, when observed, then a flame emitter sized to its bounds attaches within one frame; losing `burning` stops it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an entity transitioning from `burning` to `wet`, when observed, then a steam puff spawns once.
- AC-3 [integration] Given 30 burning objects, when the budget is exceeded, then farthest flames drop to a low LOD before any are culled.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity with both `wet` and `frozen`, when material params resolve, then frozen takes precedence per the documented order.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a greybox room with mixed element states, when three playtesters are asked what state each object is in, then they identify ≥ 90% correctly.

items.title: Destruction VFX: fracture chunks, dust and crack stages
items.description:
## Why
Smashing a wall has to look as good as it feels; crack stages make breakable things readable (Zelda-like readability).

## What
As a knight, I want smashed walls and crates to burst convincingly and cracked walls to look weak so that I know what I can break.
On `ObjectBroken`: pre-fractured chunk meshes when available, otherwise procedural box chunks for greybox; dust cloud; cosmetic debris render-only (cap 200 pieces, fade after 8 s) — gameplay rubble remains sim physics from e03. Crack stage visuals (0/1/2) for `breakable` objects so weak walls read as weak before any hit.

## Scope
- In: Chunk spawner, dust, cosmetic debris cap/fade, crack stage materials
- Out: Break rules (e04-smash-breakables)
- Out: Fractured art assets (asset group)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a weak wall broken, when processed, then chunks and a dust cloud spawn and cosmetic debris count stays ≤ 200.
- AC-2 [integration] Given crack stage 1 in sim, when rendered, then the stage-1 crack material is applied.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 250 cosmetic debris requests, when processed, then the oldest 50 are removed.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 3 simultaneous wall breaks, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High).

items.title: Spell VFX slots and templates for the spell pipeline
items.description:
## Why
Every spell should look spectacular from day one by composing templates, before bespoke art (Magic should feel magical).

## What
As a designer, I want to give a spell cast, projectile, impact, area and beam visuals by choosing templates and tints so that new spells look good without custom VFX code.
Standard slots consumed by the VFX layer: `castWindup`, `castRelease`, `projectile` (head + trail), `impact`, `area` (ring/volume sized to spell radius), `beam` (start/end sockets, width), `sustainOnTarget`, `summon`/`dissolve`. Templates for each with tint/scale params. Interface documented in docs/vfx/spell-hooks.md for the magic group.

## Scope
- In: Slot definitions, templates, docs, a demo spell in the testbed
- Out: Spell data and effects logic (e06-spell-pipeline)
- Out: Signature spell art (sorcerer/asset groups)

## Notes
Related: e06-spell-pipeline should depend on this item for visuals; not expressed here to avoid blocking VFX on the magic group.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a spell VFX block using templates only, when validated, then it passes and resolves every slot to an effect.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an area spell with radius 4 m, when it resolves, then the area template renders a ring 4 m in radius.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a beam spell, when its caster moves, then the beam start follows the cast socket every frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a spell VFX block missing an optional slot, when cast, then that slot is skipped without error.

items.title: Arrow VFX: trails, payload bursts, stuck and broken arrows
items.description:
## Why
Trick arrows need readable visuals — a splash, an unfurling rope, a rattle ring — so players understand what each did.

## What
As an archer, I want each arrow type to show clearly what it did so that trick arrows are readable.
Arrow trail (brighter for focused shots), flame on fire-arrow shafts, water burst + wet decal, rope unfurl ribbon, subtle ring pulse for noise arrows, dust for blunt impacts, deflect sparks, stuck-arrow wobble on impact, broken-arrow mesh swap when not retrievable.

## Scope
- In: Effects and cue rules for arrow events
- Out: Arrow models (asset group)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a water arrow impact, when processed, then the burst spawns and a wet decal appears matching the 1.5 m radius.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an arrow that sticks intact, when it impacts, then it wobbles for 400 ms; a broken one shows the broken mesh.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a deflected arrow, when processed, then deflect sparks spawn at the contact point.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a focused shot, when its trail spawns, then the focused trail variant is used.

items.title: World-space awareness indicators and optional noise ripples
items.description:
## Why
Stealth must be readable: players need to see who is suspicious and how noisy they were, without an all-knowing eye icon.

## What
As a thief, I want to see how aware each creature is and, optionally, how far my noise carried so that I can make informed stealth decisions.
World-space awareness indicator above creatures reflecting e11 alert states (Unaware hidden → Suspicious fill → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat), shape-coded as well as colour-coded for colour-blind players; optional last-known-position ghost marker (assist); optional noise ripple visualisation from e09 noise events (assist, off by default); extinguish puff when lights go out.

## Scope
- In: Indicators, assist visuals, colour-blind-safe shapes
- Out: Alert-state logic (e11-alert-states)
- Out: Player visibility meter HUD (stealth group)

## Notes
Related: coordinate with the stealth group's HUD so indicators and meters share a visual language.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a creature entering Suspicious with suspicion 0.4, when rendered, then its indicator shows the Suspicious shape filled 40%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature in Unaware state, when rendered, then no indicator is visible.
- AC-3 [unit] Given colour-blind simulation (deuteranopia filter), when states are compared, then every state remains distinguishable by shape alone.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the noise ripple assist off (default), when a noise event occurs, then no ripple renders.

items.title: Projected decals: scorch, frost, wet, arrow holes, cracks
items.description:
## Why
Decals leave evidence of what happened — scorch after fire, wet stone after a splash — making the world feel reactive.

## What
As a player, I want surfaces to show scorch, frost, wetness and arrow holes so that the world visibly remembers what happened.
Projected decals with a cap of 128 (High) / 48 (Low), FIFO fade-out. Wet decals match the sim `wet` duration exactly so visuals never lie about state; scorch remains after `burning` ends; frost while `frozen`; arrow holes when arrows are pulled; crack decals for crack stages.

## Scope
- In: Decal projector, cap/fade, state-synced lifetimes
- Out: Decal textures (asset group)

## Notes
Rule: a decal never conveys a gameplay state unless that state exists in the sim.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 129 decals on High, when the 129th spawns, then the oldest fades out over 1 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a surface becoming `wet` in sim for 20 s, when rendered, then the wet decal appears and is gone within one frame of the sim state clearing.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a burning object that is extinguished, when processed, then a scorch decal remains.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the Low preset, when decals spawn, then the cap is 48.

items.title: Ambient environment VFX: dust motes, embers, fireflies, fog
items.description:
## Why
Light shafts full of dust and torches spitting embers give Briar Glen and the Labyrinth their mood (visual identity).

## What
As a player, I want places to feel alive with dust, embers, fireflies and fog so that exploring is atmospheric.
Ambient effects placed via level data or derived from properties: dust motes in light shafts, torch embers and flicker (auto on `burning` light sources), fireflies (forest night), falling leaves, height fog / fog volumes, water drips and ripples. Environment effects are limited to ≤ 25% of the particle budget.

## Scope
- In: Ambient effect set, placement data, budget share
- Out: Level dressing (location epics)

## Notes
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given ambient effects requesting 40% of the particle cap, when evaluated, then they are throttled to 25%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a torch with `burning`, when loaded, then the ember effect attaches without per-torch authoring.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given an environment test scene in Chromium, when loaded, then all ambient effects render with no console errors.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the forest test scene at night, when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms on the reference machine (High).

items.title: VFX stress scene, quality tiers and auto-degrade
items.description:
## Why
Spectacle must never break frame pacing on the target hardware (hardware baseline).

## What
A combat stress scene: 12 creatures, 4 simultaneous spells, fire spreading over 10 objects, 2 destructions. Budgets added to the e32 suite. Quality tiers per preset, plus auto-degrade: when frame time exceeds budget for 2 s, halve emission rates, then disable distortion, then reduce decal cap; recover after 10 s under budget.

## Scope
- In: Stress scene, budget assertions, auto-degrade controller
- Out: Global perf suite (e32-perf-budgets)

## Notes
Cites contract baseline: High 60 fps reference machine at 1440p-equivalent; Low 60 fps at 1080p, 30 fps floor in worst-case combat on Iris Xe / base M1 class.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the stress scene on the reference machine (High), when measured for 60 s, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the stress scene on the Low preset on a base-M1-class device, when measured, then frame rate never drops below 30 fps.
- AC-3 [unit] Given frame time over budget for 2 s, when the controller evaluates, then emission rates halve; after 10 s under budget, they restore.
- AC-4 [unit] Given frame time spikes shorter than 2 s, when evaluated, then no degradation occurs.
